## Limit fixtures

D-90, accepted on 2026-09-25. Every case is a project of one composition 6 by 2 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/limits/`: one of the adjustment fixtures' drawings, `bg` or `dot`, with an adjustment layer above it holding one effect. Values are linear premultiplied working values; each cell is red, green, blue and alpha.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/limits_reference.py`**, which works each setting's value at the frame from document 20, holds it inside its range, and renders each pixel from document 21 through `tools/adjust_reference.py`, summing the blur in two dimensions at once. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/limits/expected_limits.json`. At 20 stops a value is about a million and at sigma 500 about a millionth, so the tolerance is relative: a sample agrees when it is within 1e-4 of the expected value's own size, and exactly when the expected value is 0. FX-LIMIT-006 to 010 hold a value past a limit: the file is read, the effect is kept as written, and every frame is the drawing's own, with the warning `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID` (D-46).

Commands, D-46: setting a blur's sigma to 501 is refused with "A Gaussian blur's sigma runs from 0 to 500, and this is 501.", and to -1 with "A Gaussian blur's sigma runs from 0 to 500, and this is -1."; setting exposure to 21 stops is refused with "Exposure runs from -20 to 20 stops, and this is 21.", and to -21 with "Exposure runs from -20 to 20 stops, and this is -21.". Each refusal leaves the effect, the document revision and the undo stack as they were. Sigma 500, 20 stops and -20 stops are accepted.

## Line recolour fixtures

D-91, accepted on 2026-09-25. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/recolor/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.line_recolor` on it; the drawing is `Fixtures/recolor/media/face.png`: a box of line `#1e1a24` in columns 2 to 13 and rows 2 to 7, filled with skin `#f6d6be`, with the line at half covering down its left side in column 1, its antialiased edge, and a red trace line `#c82828` across row 5, columns 4 to 11. Unless the case says: the line chosen, tolerance 0, new colour `#ff0000`. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/recolor_reference.py`**, which works D-91's rule in double precision. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/recolor/expected_recolor.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: in FX-RECOLOR-001 exactly the 38 pixels of line change, the half-covering edge to red at half covering; no colour, a colour one step off at tolerance 0, and the line's own colour as the new one leave the drawing exactly (002, 003, 009); tolerance 1 and capitals give 001 (004, 006); the keyed tolerance chooses nothing below 10 and the line from 10 (007); and at tolerance 255 every pixel that shows turns red at its own covering (011).

## Directional blur fixtures

D-92, accepted on 2026-09-25, its rule changed by D-98 the same day. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/directional_blur/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.directional_blur` on it; the drawing is `Fixtures/directional_blur/media/bars.png`: a line `#1e1a24` down its left edge, column 0, rows 2 to 7; a block of skin `#f6d6be` in columns 5 to 9 and rows 3 to 6; and one red pixel `#c82828` at half covering at (12, 4). Unless the case says: direction 0, length 4. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/directional_blur_reference.py`**, which works D-98's rule in double precision. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/directional_blur/expected_directional_blur.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**D-98 changed** 001 to 004 and 007 to 011 when the owner accepted it on 2026-09-25; 005, 006 and 012 to 015 are unchanged. D-92's first values are retired, kept in the repository's history at commit ca2be49.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: at direction 0 the block's row 4 is 3.875 fifths covered and nothing spreads sideways, at 90 the reverse, and the block's covering is kept (001, 002); the opposite direction and ten turns give the same (003, 008); length 0 leaves the drawing exactly (005); length 1 covers the edge column three quarters and the one outside a quarter (006); length 2.5 reaches a fifteenth two columns out (007); moved right, the line streaks into the grown border (009); and the keyed length and direction pass through the fixed cases (010, 011).

## Select colour fixtures

D-93, accepted on 2026-09-25. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/select_color/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.select_color` on it; the drawing is line recolour's, `Fixtures/select_color/media/face.png`: a box of line `#1e1a24` in columns 2 to 13 and rows 2 to 7, filled with skin `#f6d6be`, with the line at half covering down its left side in column 1 and a red trace line `#c82828` across row 5, columns 4 to 11. Unless the case says: the line chosen, tolerance 0, keep `chosen`. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/select_color_reference.py`**, which works D-93's rule in double precision. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/select_color/expected_select_color.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: keep chosen and keep others split the drawing between them pixel for pixel, the half-covering edge kept at half (001, 002); no colour leaves the drawing exactly, whichever is kept (003, 004); the trace line chosen too keeps it (005); capitals choose the same (006); the keyed tolerance keeps nothing until it reaches 10 (007); moved, the same frame moves (008); and tolerance 255 with keep others leaves nothing (009).

## Line width fixtures

D-94, accepted on 2026-09-25. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/line_width/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.line_width` on it; the drawing is line recolour's, `Fixtures/line_width/media/face.png`: a box of line `#1e1a24` in columns 2 to 13 and rows 2 to 7, filled with skin `#f6d6be`, with the line at half covering down its left side in column 1 and a red trace line `#c82828` across row 5, columns 4 to 11. Unless the case says: width 1, based on the shape, the line listed as a colour, tolerance 0. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/line_width_reference.py`**, which works D-94's rule in double precision at every pixel of the composition. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/line_width/expected_line_width.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: width 1 grows the drawing one pixel with square-cut corners, the half-covering edge turning solid and a new one outside it (001); 1.5 fills the corners (002); -1 clears the outer line and leaves the next line half covering in its own colour (003); width 0 leaves the drawing exactly (004); the chosen line grows into skin and outside but leaves the trace line alone (005); a one-pixel line thinned by one is gone, taking the skin above it (006); the trace line grown by two covers five rows (007); the keyed width passes through FX-WIDTH-001 (008); moved, the same frame moves (009); no colour or shape with colours listed change nothing beyond the shape's own result (010, 011); and width -20 leaves nothing (012).

FX-WIDTH-001: Shape, width 1: the drawing grows one pixel up, down, left and right. The half-covering edge in column 1 becomes solid line, and a new half-covering edge appears in column 0; the corners stay square-cut.

## Radial blur fixtures

D-95, accepted on 2026-09-25. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/radial_blur/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.radial_blur` on it; the drawing is directional blur's, `Fixtures/radial_blur/media/bars.png`: a line `#1e1a24` down column 0, rows 2 to 7, a block of skin `#f6d6be` in columns 5 to 9 and rows 3 to 6, and one red pixel `#c82828` at half covering at (12, 4). Unless the case says: spin, amount 30, centre 50, 50, which is the point (8, 5). Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/radial_blur_reference.py`**, which works D-95's rule in double precision at every pixel of the composition. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/radial_blur/expected_radial_blur.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. FX-RADIAL-012's directional blur follows D-98's rule since 2026-09-25, which moved 138 of its pixels by at most 0.017; its first values are retired. The zoom smears outward only since D-110, proposed on 2026-09-26, which moved 86, 81 and 154 pixels of FX-RADIAL-002, 005 and 007 by at most 0.333, 0.344 and 0.452, and 160 of FX-EDGES-008's by at most 0.247; their first values are retired.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: the middle of the block stays solid under a spin or a zoom; the spin smears the line up and down past its ends and hardly sideways (001); the zoom smears the block outward on both sides and nothing inward, so the column inside the line stays empty (002); amount 0 leaves the drawing exactly (003); the far corner's arcs differ (004); about (4, 5) everything smears away from the centre and the three columns between the line and the centre stay empty (005); the most smears further, the zoom to a pixel four past the block that 30 does not reach (006, 007); the keyed amount and centre pass through their plain cases (008, 009); moved, the same frame moves and nothing is drawn left of the drawing (010); every pixel of 011 takes 256 samples; and after a directional blur the spin turns about the drawing's corner, not the grown layer's (012).

FX-RADIAL-001: Spin 30 about the middle: every edge smears round the centre, the further out the longer, and the middle of the block stays solid.

## Bloom fixtures

D-96, accepted on 2026-09-25. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/bloom/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.bloom` on it; the drawing is glow's three patches, `Fixtures/bloom/media/patches.png`, in rows 3 to 6: yellow `#fadc78` in columns 2 to 4, whose brightest channel is 98 %, brown `#996633` in 7 and 8, exactly 60 %, and purple `#3c286e` in 11 to 13, 43 %; `faint.png` is the same half covering. Unless the case says: threshold 80, radius 4, intensity 1, streaks none, length 6, angle 0. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/bloom_reference.py`**, which works D-96's rule, its streaks read along D-98's lines, in double precision at every pixel of the composition, summing each blur in two dimensions at once. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/bloom/expected_bloom.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**D-98 changed** 007, 008, 011, 016 and 019, the streaks off the quarter turns or of a length that is not a whole number, when the owner accepted it on 2026-09-25; 009 now equals 006 exactly, and the other 22 are unchanged. D-96's first values are retired, kept in the repository's history at commit ca2be49.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: only the yellow blooms at threshold 80, the halo reaching the brown and not the purple, and it is tighter than glow's at the same radius, more light on the yellow and less round it (001); intensity 0 and threshold 100 leave the drawing exactly (002, 004); radius 0 adds each yellow pixel onto itself (003); the cross lights the pixels above and beside the yellow and not those off its corners, the star lights the diagonals too and is exactly the average of the cross at 0 and at 45 degrees, and the cross at 90 is the cross at 0 (006 to 009); radius 20 lights every pixel (010); the colour passes white at intensity 2.5 (012); half covering halves the halo (013); the keyed settings pass through their plain cases (014 to 017); moved, the same frame moves and the streak past the left edge shows (018); and neither radius nor length is rounded (019).

## Colour key fixtures

D-97, accepted on 2026-09-25. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/color_key/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.color_key` on it; the drawing, `Fixtures/color_key/media/screen.png`, is a figure in front of a green screen: the screen `#00b140` everywhere, except column 0, empty; column 15, the screen at half covering; rows 8 and 9, its shadow `#006424`; and a box of line `#1e1a24` in columns 5 to 10 and rows 2 to 7 filled with skin `#f6d6be`, with a grey button `#808080` at (7, 4) and green spill `#5aa064` down column 4 beside it. Unless the case says: the green chosen, tolerance 0, softness 0, match `rgb`. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/color_key_reference.py`**, which works D-97's rule in double precision. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/color_key/expected_color_key.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: tolerance 0 takes exactly the green pixels, the half-covering edge included (001); tolerance 80 takes the shadow and not the spill (002); in the band a pixel keeps exactly its share, colour and covering alike (003, 009); hue takes the shadow with the screen and keeps the spill, the figure and the grey (004), and the spill's share in the band (005); no colour leaves the drawing exactly (006, 007); the keyed tolerance takes nothing more at 50, and the shadow and the spill at 100 (008); two colours take both (010); capitals take the same (011); a grey chosen takes only the button by `rgb` (012), nothing by `hue` below 255 (013) and everything at 255 (014); moved, the same frame moves (015). It also checks the hue itself: red is 0, blue 240, and two reds either side of 0 are less than a degree apart.

FX-KEY-001: The screen's green chosen, tolerance 0: the screen goes, its half-covering right edge too; the shadow, the spill and the figure stay.

## Repeat edge pixels fixtures

D-109, proposed on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/edges/`, holding one drawing the same size with one or two blurs on it, each of Gaussian Blur, Directional Blur and Radial Blur with `edges` `"repeat"` unless the case says. The drawings are `Fixtures/edges/media/plate.png`, a picture to the layer's edges, fully covered, whose pixel (x, y) is `(16x, 25y, 160)` in 8 bits, and directional blur's `bars.png`. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/edges_reference.py`**, which works D-109's rule in double precision at every pixel of the composition: Directional Blur and Radial Blur by `tools/directional_blur_reference.py`'s and `tools/radial_blur_reference.py`'s rules with their `edges` argument, and Gaussian Blur by document 21's, summed in two dimensions at once. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/edges/expected_edges.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: with repeat, every pixel of the picture stays fully covered under each blur (001, 004, 005, 007, 008), where written `"transparent"` it fades exactly as a file without the setting (002); the middle, out of reach of the edges, is blurred exactly as without it (001, 004); moved, nothing is drawn left of the drawing, because the layer does not grow (003, 006); the line on the bars' edge keeps more of itself than FX-DIRBLUR-009's (006); and a spin after a Directional Blur repeats the edge of the grown layer it is given (009).

FX-EDGES-001: Gaussian Blur, sigma 1, edges repeat, on a picture that fills the layer: every pixel stays fully covered, the edges as solid as the middle, and the middle is blurred exactly as without it.

## Curves fixtures

D-111, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/curves/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Curves on it, its four curves `master`, `red`, `green` and `blue` the default `[[0, 0], [255, 255]]` unless the case says. The drawing is `media/chart.png`, a colour chart 16 by 10 with empty pixels round it: rows of line, of skin `#f6d6be` and its shadow `#dca08c` each ending in a half-covering pixel, a grey ramp from 0 to 255, red, blue, green, skin, shadow, white and black whole and at half covering, and skin and red at coverings 32 to 224. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/curves_reference.py`**, which works D-111's rule in double precision at every pixel: each channel of a pixel that shows, as a 0..255 encoded straight colour, through its own curve and then the master, each the natural cubic spline through its points and flat outside them, the result held inside 0..255. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/curves/expected_curves.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every pixel that shows is its drawn 8-bit channels through the case's curves at its own covering, and every empty pixel stays empty (002 to 013); the default and three points on the straight line give the drawing (001, 012); a curve is flat outside its end points (004); a spline that swings past 0 or 255 is held (005, 006); a channel's own curve runs before the master (007); an inverting master leaves the empty pixels empty and the soft ones soft (008); and a moved layer is the same, moved (014).

FX-CURVES-001: All four curves the default, [[0, 0], [255, 255]]: the drawing, untouched.

## Levels fixtures

D-112, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/levels/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Levels on it, its settings `input_black` 0, `input_white` 255, `gamma` 1, `output_black` 0 and `output_white` 255 unless the case says. The drawing is Curves' `media/chart.png`, a colour chart 16 by 10 with empty pixels round it: rows of line, of skin `#f6d6be` and its shadow `#dca08c` each ending in a half-covering pixel, a grey ramp from 0 to 255, red, blue, green, skin, shadow, white and black whole and at half covering, and skin and red at coverings 32 to 224. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/levels_reference.py`**, which works D-112's rule in double precision at every pixel: each channel of a pixel that shows, as a 0..255 encoded straight colour, from the input range to 0..1 and held there, raised to 1 / gamma, and laid on the output range. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/levels/expected_levels.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every pixel that shows is its drawn 8-bit channels through the case's levels at its own covering, and every empty pixel stays empty (002 to 016); the defaults give the drawing (001); input black and white clip the ramp's ends (002, 003); gamma bends the middle both ways (004, 005, 016); either range reversed inverts, the two the same (009, 010); equal input black and white is a threshold (011); keyed settings are worked at each frame and held inside their ranges (013 to 015); and a moved layer is the same, moved (017).

FX-LEVELS-001: Every setting its default, 0, 255, gamma 1, 0, 255: the drawing, within the tolerance.

Frame 0:

Every pixel is the drawing's, unchanged.

FX-LEVELS-002: Input black 64: the ramp's greys at or below 64 become black, and every colour darkens toward it; white stays.

## Hue/Saturation fixtures

D-113, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/hue_saturation/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Hue/Saturation on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/hue_saturation/media/bands.png`: rows 0 and 9 and column 0 empty, and between them columns in pairs of pure red 1-2, pure green 3-4, pure blue 5-6, grey `#808080` 7-8, skin `#f6d6be` 9-10, magenta `#ff00ff` 11-12 and line `#1e1a24` 13-14, and the skin at half covering in column 15. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/hue_saturation_reference.py`**, which works D-113's rule in double precision at every pixel of the composition, on each shown pixel's straight colour through the sRGB curve read as hue, saturation and lightness. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/hue_saturation/expected_hue_saturation.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: the primaries trade places under a third of a turn and the grey stays (002, 003); red goes below 0 to 330 and magenta past 360 to 30 (004, 005); saturation -100 leaves every pixel grey, and +100 holds the skin at full saturation while the primaries stay (007, 008); lightness +100 and -100 turn every shown pixel white and black at its own covering (010, 011); half a turn either way is the same (015); keyed saturation passes through the drawing at 0 (016); moved, the frame is the same, moved (017). In every case the empty pixels stay empty and the soft edge keeps its half covering.

FX-HUESAT-001: All three at 0, the defaults: the drawing, untouched.

Frame 0: every pixel is the drawing's, unchanged.

FX-HUESAT-002: Hue +120: red turns green, green blue, and blue red; magenta, at 300, goes past 360 to 60, yellow; the grey and the empty pixels stay as they are, and the soft edge keeps its half covering.

## Gradient fixtures

D-114, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/gradient/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Gradient (`core.gradient`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/gradient/media/cel.png`, a cel: a box of line #1e1a24 in columns 2 to 14 and rows 1 to 8, filled with skin #f6d6be, its columns 10 to 13 in shadow #dca08c, with the line at half covering down column 1 as its antialiased edge; column 0, column 15 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/gradient_reference.py`**, which works D-114's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/gradient/expected_gradient.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering and leaves the empty pixels empty (all); multiply darkens row by row, every pixel in a row alike (001); normal at 100 paints the gradient itself (002), screen only lightens (003), add stays within the covering (004); radial rings reach #6450a0 at eight pixels (005); start and end the same paint the end colour everywhere (006); points outside the drawing give the middle third (008) or only the start (009); the keyed start point and opacities meet the plain cases at their frames (010, 011); opacity 0 and capitals change nothing (012, 014); and moved, the gradient moves with the drawing (015).

FX-GRAD-001: The settings as they start: linear from the top middle to the bottom middle, white at 0 per cent to #6450a0 at 50, multiply. Row 1, the line along the top, is barely touched, and each row down is darker and more violet, the bottom most; every pixel in a row is changed alike, and the empty pixels stay empty.

## Drop shadow fixtures

D-115, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/drop_shadow/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.drop_shadow` on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/drop_shadow/media/card.png`, a box of line `#1e1a24` in columns 5 to 9 and rows 3 to 6 filled with skin `#f6d6be`, with the line at half covering (128 of 255) at (10, 4), its antialiased edge, and the rest empty, so there is room round it for what the effect adds to show in the frame. The layer grows by the distance rounded up and the softness's blur reach, and the frame shows the grown pixels in place, cut off at its edges. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/drop_shadow_reference.py`**, which works D-115's rule in double precision at every pixel of the grown layer: the drawing's covering blurred by document 21's Gaussian at softness / 3 (`tools/edges_reference.py`'s), read back by document 21's bilinear sample (`tools/radial_blur_reference.py`'s) `distance` pixels against the direction, and laid behind the drawing. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/drop_shadow/expected_drop_shadow.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: a pixel the card covers fully never changes (every case); straight across or down by a whole number of pixels the shadow is the covering moved exactly, at half covering in black (002 to 005, 013, 017), and direction -270 is 90 (006); slantwise it is spread by the bilinear sample (001); at distance 0 it shows only through the soft pixel and the layer does not grow (007), and with softness it fades outward on every side (008, 009); opacity 0 changes nothing (010); a colour shows its exact straight colour where the shadow is whole, in capitals the same (011, 012); keyed settings match the cases they pass through, and an opacity eased past 100 is held at 100 (013 to 015); and moved, or thrown upward, the shadow is cut off by the frame's edge (016, 017).

FX-SHADOW-001: The defaults: black at 50 per cent, direction 135, distance 5, softness 0. The card's shadow falls down and to the right, 3.54 pixels each way, spread by the bilinear sample over the pixels it falls between; where it lies wholly under the card's shape it is black at half covering. The card itself, fully covered, is unchanged, and the shadow's lower part falls below the frame.

## Lens blur fixtures

D-116, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/lens_blur/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.lens_blur` on it. The drawings are `Fixtures/lens_blur/media/bars.png`, directional blur's: a line down the left edge, column 0, rows 2 to 7, `#1e1a24`; a block of skin `#f6d6be` in columns 5 to 9 and rows 3 to 6; and one red pixel `#c82828` at half covering (128) at (12, 4), the rest empty, so a blur has room to spread inside the frame; and `plate.png`, the edges fixtures' picture to the layer's edges, fully covered, whose pixel (x, y) is `(16x, 25y, 160)` in 8 bits. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/lens_blur_reference.py`**, which works D-116's rule in double precision at every pixel of the composition: the plain mean of the premultiplied pixels at the whole-pixel offsets within the radius, reading transparent outside the layer and growing it by the radius rounded up, or, with `edges` `"repeat"`, holding each offset's column and row inside the layer and not growing. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/lens_blur/expected_lens_blur.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: the disc holds 1, 5, 9, 13, 21, 49 and 317 pixels at radius 0.9, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 4 and 10; radius 0 and 0.9 change nothing (002, 003); at radius 1 the block's edge pixels lose a fifth for each empty neighbour and the pixel off its corner stays empty (004), which radius 1.5 reaches with a ninth (005); the red pixel spreads to an even patch of 1/49 at radius 4 (007); with repeat the picture stays fully covered and its middle is blurred as with transparent (008, 009); a keyed radius is worked at each frame and an eased one held at 0 (010, 011); moved, the grown column left of the line shows and, with repeat, nothing is drawn left of the drawing (012, 013).

FX-LENS-001: The settings as they start, radius 10, edges transparent: every pixel is the mean of the 317 within ten pixels of it, so the line, the block and the red pixel spread into one faint even haze over the whole frame.

## Rim light fixtures

D-117, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/rim_light/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.rim_light` on it. The drawing is `Fixtures/rim_light/media/figure.png`: a block of skin `#f6d6be` in columns 3 to 12 and rows 2 to 7, its foot, row 7, the line `#1e1a24`; the skin at half covering (128) down column 2 beside it, a soft edge; and a red dot `#c82828` alone at (14, 5), the rest empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change by more than 1e-12 are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, the few inside the block that the light does not reach differing from it by rounding alone.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/rim_light_reference.py`**, which works D-117's rule in double precision at every pixel of the composition: document 21's Gaussian blur of the layer's covering at softness / 3 on the grid grown by its radius, sampled bilinearly `width` pixels from each covered pixel's centre toward the light, one minus it the rim, and the pixel's straight colour moved toward the blend's colour by the rim times the intensity, its covering kept. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/rim_light/expected_rim_light.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: in every case the empty pixels stay exactly empty and every covering is kept; the lit side follows the direction, 45 the top and right (001), 0, 90, 180 and 270 the top, right, foot and left, exactly (002 to 005), 450 as 90 (020); the red dot shades what lies three pixels from it toward the light (001, 003); width 0 at softness 0 lights only the soft edge, by 127/255 (006); softness 0 gives a hard rim (009); intensity 0 changes nothing and 50 is exactly halfway (010, 011); each blend's lit dot is its formula of the colour (012 to 015), add passing white where screen does not, and capitals are the same colour (016); keyed direction and width are worked at each frame and an eased intensity held at 100 (017 to 019); moved, the same, moved (021).

FX-RIM-001: The settings as they start: white light from 45 degrees, the upper right, width 3, softness 1, intensity 100, normal. The block's top two rows and right two columns turn white, with a fainter third; the red dot, alone, turns wholly white, and itself shades the line's end at (12, 7), whose point toward the light falls beside the dot; the empty pixels stay empty and the block's lower left stays skin.

## Outline fixtures

D-118, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/outline/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.outline` on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is drop shadow's, `Fixtures/outline/media/card.png`, a box of line `#1e1a24` in columns 5 to 9 and rows 3 to 6 filled with skin `#f6d6be`, with the line at half covering (128 of 255) at (10, 4), its antialiased edge, and the rest empty, so there is room round it for what the effect adds to show in the frame. A positive width grows the layer by the width rounded up and the softness's blur reach, and the frame shows the grown pixels in place, cut off at its edges. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/outline_reference.py`**, which works D-118's rule in double precision at every pixel of the grown layer: the greatest covering over the whole steps within the width, blurred by document 21's Gaussian at softness / 3 (`tools/edges_reference.py`'s), and laid behind the drawing. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/outline/expected_outline.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: a pixel the card covers fully never changes (every case); every empty pixel within the width of the card, counted on whole steps, is the colour at full covering and every other is empty, so width 1 leaves the corners empty and 2.5 reaches (2, 1) but not (2, 2) or (3, 0), with the layer's outermost ring empty (001, 004, 005, 010, 013); width 0 changes nothing, even with softness (002, 003); softness fades the band outward (006); opacity scales it (007); the soft pixel takes the band through its uncovered share, and past it the band is only as strong as the soft pixel (001, 004, 008, 012); in capitals a colour is the same (009); keyed settings match the cases they pass through, and an opacity eased past 100 is held at 100 (010, 011); and moved, or wide, the band is cut off by the frame's edges (013, 014).

FX-OUTLINE-001: The defaults: white, width 3, softness 0, opacity 100. A white band three pixels wide round the card, its corners rounded (a pixel three across and one down from a corner is outside it), filling rows 0 to 9; the card itself, fully covered, is unchanged. The soft pixel takes the white through its uncovered share and is fully covered; past it, where only the soft pixel is within reach, as at (13, 4), the band is only as strong as it, 128/255.

## Noise fixtures

D-119, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/noise/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Noise on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/noise/media/card.png`: column 0 and row 9 empty, column 15 the skin `#f6d6be` at half covering, and on a grey `#808080` card a box of line `#1e1a24` in columns 3 to 12 and rows 1 to 7 filled with skin, with a white patch in columns 5 to 6 and a black one in columns 9 to 10, both in rows 3 to 4. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/noise_reference.py`**, which works D-119's rule in double precision at every pixel of the composition, with the grain's hash worked on Python's whole numbers held to 64 bits. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/noise/expected_noise.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: animated, the grain differs on frames 0, 2 and 4, and not animated it is the same on all three (001, 002); mono moves the three channels together and color each its own way (001, 003); two seeds differ, and seed 3.7 is seed 3 (004 to 006, 011); amount 0 changes nothing (008); at amount 100 white is held at white where the grain would lighten it and black at black where it would darken it (009); twice the amount is twice the step (010); and moved, each frame's grain moves with the drawing (012). In every case the empty pixels stay empty and the soft edge keeps its half covering.

FX-NOISE-001: The defaults, amount 10, mono, seed 0, animated: every shown pixel's three channels move together by up to 0.05 through the sRGB curve, and the grain is different on frames 0, 2 and 4; the empty pixels stay empty and the soft edge keeps its half covering.

## Chromatic Aberration fixtures

D-120, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/chromatic_aberration/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Chromatic Aberration (`core.chromatic_aberration`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/chromatic_aberration/media/figure.png`: a white block in columns 0 to 5 and rows 2 to 7, against the drawing's left edge, closed by a line #1e1a24 down column 6, and a skin block #f6d6be in columns 9 to 12 and rows 3 to 6 with a half-covering edge down column 13; everything else is empty. The drawing's half diagonal is sqrt(16^2 + 10^2) / 2 = 9.434. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/chromatic_aberration_reference.py`**, which works D-120's rule in double precision at every pixel, sampling by `tools/radial_blur_reference.py`'s bilinear rule. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/chromatic_aberration/expected_chromatic_aberration.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: green is always the pixel's own (all); amount 0 changes nothing (002, 005 frame 0); red fringes outward with the red sample's covering, blue inward, and the left column on the layer's edge loses its blue and nothing is drawn outside the layer (001, 007); the covering is never less than the pixel's own (001, 003); about the left edge, red runs right and the left column keeps its blue (004); keyed amount and centre meet the plain cases at their frames (005, 006); the most, or a centre far off, keeps only the green (008, 009); at amount 1 the insides of the blocks keep their colour (010); and about the bottom right corner red reaches above the blocks and blue below (011).

FX-CHROMA-001: The settings as they start, amount 3 about the middle: red fringes outward past the blocks' outer edges, where the red sample alone covers and the pixel takes its covering, and blue fringes inward; the white block's left column, on the layer's edge, loses its blue, whose sample falls outside the layer, and turns yellow, and nothing is drawn beyond the layer.

## Distance Gradation fixtures

D-123, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/distance_gradation/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Distance Gradation (`core.distance_gradation`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/distance_gradation/media/block.png`: a block in rows 1 to 8, against the drawing's left edge, skin #f6d6be in columns 0 to 6 and shadow #dca08c in columns 7 to 9, with a hole, an empty pixel, at (4, 4); its soft right edge is the skin at half covering (128) down column 10, which counts as in, and at a quarter covering (64) down column 11, which counts as out but shows; and a red dot #c82828 alone at (14, 4). Rows 0 and 9 and the rest are empty. The furthest pixel from any out pixel is (7, 5), sqrt 10 from the hole. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/distance_gradation_reference.py`**, which works D-123's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, with Gradient's blend mix (`tools/gradient_reference.py`). The same numbers are in `Fixtures/distance_gradation/expected_distance_gradation.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: its distances equal those found against every out pixel, the layer's edge counting as out (all); every case keeps every pixel's covering and leaves the empty pixels empty (all); the shading is strongest at the edge and weakest at (7, 5) (001); width 2 reaches three quarters at the edge and leaves exactly the ten pixels 2.5 or more in untouched (002); width 1 shades a neighbour of an out pixel by half and a diagonal one by 1.5 - sqrt 2 (003); width 0.5 shades only the quarter-covered column (004); width 0, with or without invert, opacity 0 and white multiply change nothing (005, 006, 007, 013); invert gives one less the plain strength (008, 009); normal stays at half strength, screen only lightens, add passes screen (010, 011, 012); capitals change nothing (014); the keyed width and the held, overshooting opacity meet the plain cases at their frames (015, 016); and moved, the shading moves with the drawing (017).

FX-DISTGRAD-001: The settings as they start: #6450a0, width 10, opacity 50, invert off, multiply. Every pixel that shows is darkened toward violet, the most along the block's edge, the dot and the quarter-covered column, and less at each pixel further in, and the least at (7, 5), sqrt 10 from the hole, the furthest from any out pixel; the empty pixels stay empty.

## Light Rays fixtures

D-124, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/light_rays/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Light Rays (`core.light_rays`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/light_rays/media/lamp.png`: a warm yellow block #fadc78 (brightest channel 250, 98 %) in columns 5 to 7 and rows 3 to 6, left of the middle, with the same yellow at half covering down column 4 as its soft edge; a brown block #996633 (brightest channel 153, exactly 60 %) in columns 10 and 11, rows 3 to 6, right of the middle; and a purple line #3c286e (43 %) down column 14, rows 2 to 7; everything else is empty. The centre 50, 50 is the point (8, 5), on the yellow's right edge. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/light_rays_reference.py`**, which works D-124's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, testing the light with `tools/glow_reference.py`'s bright test (D-89) and streaking it with `tools/radial_blur_reference.py`'s zoom (D-95 with D-110). The same numbers are in `Fixtures/light_rays/expected_light_rays.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: nothing is ever taken away and the covering stays inside 0 to 1 (all); the yellow's light streaks outward into the empty pixels, fading, and columns 9 to 15 are untouched (001); intensity 0 and threshold 100 change nothing (002, 004); length 0 adds each lit pixel onto itself and doubles the soft edge to full covering (003); at threshold 60 the brown streams right over the purple (005); length 100 reaches every pixel (006); intensity 2.5 is two and a half times the rays, past white (007); an orange colour tints them and black adds covering but no colour (008, 009); capitals change nothing (010); about the top left corner the rays run down and right, and from above straight down with nothing above the yellow (011, 012); the keyed length, threshold and centre meet the plain cases at their frames, and an eased intensity that overshoots is held at 10 (013 to 016); and moved, the rays move with the drawing and nothing is drawn left of it (017).

FX-RAYS-001: The settings as they start: centre 50, 50, the point (8, 5), length 50, threshold 70, intensity 1, white. Only the yellow, 98 %, is bright enough; its light streaks outward, away from the centre: left across its soft edge into the empty columns 0 to 3, and up and down into the empty rows above and below it, fading as it goes, and it brightens the yellow itself. The brown, 60 %, and the purple give no light, and columns 9 to 15 are untouched; nothing is drawn past the layer's edge.

## Exposure Flicker fixtures

D-125, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/exposure_flicker/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Exposure Flicker (`core.exposure_flicker`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/exposure_flicker/media/card.png`, Noise's card: column 0 and row 9 empty, column 15 the skin `#f6d6be` at half covering, and on a grey `#808080` card a box of line `#1e1a24` in columns 3 to 12 and rows 1 to 7 filled with skin, with a white patch in columns 5 to 6 and a black one in columns 9 to 10, both in rows 3 to 4. The frame number the effect reads is the composition frame, never saved. Values are linear premultiplied working values. Every frame is the drawing, moved as the case moves it, with every pixel's red, green and blue times one factor, 2^stops, and alpha unchanged, so each frame is one line giving its stops and factor, or naming an earlier frame it equals exactly. Three frames are listed pixel by pixel, the pixels that change only (every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly): FX-FLICKER-001's frame 0, FX-FLICKER-004's frame 1, whose white passes its covering, and FX-FLICKER-015's frame 0, moved.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/exposure_flicker_reference.py`**, which works D-125's rule in double precision at every pixel of the composition, with the frame's number from Noise's hash (`tools/noise_reference.py`, imported) worked on Python's whole numbers held to 64 bits. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/exposure_flicker/expected_exposure_flicker.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

## Gradient Map fixtures

D-129, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/gradient_map/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Gradient Map (`core.gradient_map`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/gradient_map/media/swatches.png`: a box of line #1e1a24 in columns 2 to 14 and rows 1 to 8 holding, in rows 2 to 7, skin #f6d6be in columns 3 to 5, shadow #dca08c in 6 to 8, red #c82828 in 9 and 10, white in 11, blue #4060ff in 12 and black in 13; down its left side, column 1, the line at half covering in rows 1 to 4 and the skin at half covering in rows 5 to 8; column 0, column 15 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. Their brightness, t, is 0.1087 (line), 0.8619 (skin), 0.6818 (shadow), 0.4093 (red), 1 (white), 0.4452 (blue) and 0 (black). Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/gradient_map_reference.py`**, which works D-129's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/gradient_map/expected_gradient_map.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering and leaves the empty pixels empty (all); the start settings turn every pixel grey, white and black kept, the skin lightest and the line darkest, a half-covering pixel the same grey as its colour (001); amount 0 changes nothing (002) and amount 50 is halfway (003); the sunset ramp paints black and white its end colours exactly (004); midpoint 25 lightens and 75 darkens everything between black and white (005, 006), and 1 and 99 put it all on one half of the ramp (007, 008); one colour three times paints it everywhere (009); the ramp turned over makes a negative (010); a red midtone reddens only what lies between (011); the keyed midpoint and amount meet the plain cases at their frames, and an overshooting ease is held at 100 (012 to 014); capitals change nothing (015); and moved, the map moves with the drawing (016).

FX-GRADMAP-001: The settings as they start: black, #808080 at the midpoint 50, white, amount 100. Every pixel that shows turns grey by its brightness, red, green and blue alike: the white stays white, the black stays black, the skin is the lightest of the rest and the line the darkest; a pixel at half covering takes the same grey as its colour at full covering, at its own covering, and the empty pixels stay empty.

## Color Balance fixtures

D-130, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/color_balance/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Color Balance (`core.color_balance`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/color_balance/media/tones.png`: bands of tone from dark to light, two columns each, in rows 1 to 8, black #000000 in columns 1 and 2, the line #1e1a24 in 3 and 4, a dark grey #404040 in 5 and 6, a grey #808080 in 7 and 8, a light grey #c0c0c0 in 9 and 10, skin #f6d6be in 11 and 12 and white #ffffff in 13 and 14, with the skin at half covering in column 15 as a soft edge; column 0 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. Black takes only the shadows and white only the highlights; the dark grey shares about half and half between the shadows and the midtones, the light grey between the midtones and the highlights, and the grey, a hair above half brightness, takes nearly all midtones. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/color_balance_reference.py`**, which works D-130's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/color_balance/expected_color_balance.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering, leaves the empty pixels empty, and grades the soft edge as the skin at half covering (all); all nine at 0 change nothing (001, 012 frame 2); shadows move black the most, half the scale at 100, and the dark tones less, and leave everything at or above half brightness alone (002, 003), with black held at 0 when pushed down (003); midtones move the grey the most and leave black and white alone (004, 005); highlights hold a full white channel at the top and move a white one down half the scale (006, 007); all three together lift every tone half the scale (008); split tones reach the dark and light greys and barely touch the grey (009), and the dark grey takes about half of each of two tones (010); the keyed triples meet the plain cases at their frames, an overshooting ease held at -100 (011 to 013); and moved, the effect moves with the drawing (014).

Frame 0: every pixel is the drawing's, unchanged.

## Offset fixtures

D-131, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/offset/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Offset (`core.offset`) on it, unmoved unless the case says; FX-OFFSET-017 and 018 put a Drop Shadow (`core.drop_shadow`: black, opacity 100, direction 90, distance 2, softness 0) ahead of it, which grows the layer two pixels on every side, to 20 by 14. The drawing is `Fixtures/offset/media/tile.png`, a tile touching the drawing's edges so the wrap shows: a white block in columns 0 to 4 and rows 1 to 4, against the left edge, closed by a line #1e1a24 down column 5; a skin block #f6d6be in columns 9 to 13 and rows 5 to 9, against the bottom edge, with a half-covering edge down column 14; and one red dot #c82828 in the top right corner, (15, 0); everything else is empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/offset_reference.py`**, which works D-131's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, and for FX-OFFSET-017 and 018 takes the drop shadow from `tools/drop_shadow_reference.py`. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/offset/expected_offset.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: with the layer the frame's size, each channel's total over the frame is the drawing's, nothing lost or gained (001 to 015); whole-pixel shifts move every pixel exactly, wrapping, against a copy written out by hand (002 to 009), right, down, left and up, the quarters changed corner to corner (005), and a whole width and height, the most, or any number of turns round changing nothing or the same as the small shift (006 to 009); half a pixel is the even mix of each pixel and its left neighbour round the wrap (010); a part-pixel shift both ways mixes four pixels at 9/16, 3/16, 3/16 and 1/16 (011), and nearly twice round is the same as the small shift exactly (012); keyed shifts meet the plain cases at their frames, whole and part-pixel (013, 014); an eased key past 100000 is held there and changes nothing where unheld it would slide four pixels (015); moved, nothing wraps into the columns left of the layer (016); and after a drop shadow the wrap goes round the grown 20 by 14 layer, so 16 slides four pixels left and 20, 14 leaves the drop shadow's frame as it was (017, 018).

FX-OFFSET-001: The settings as they start, shift 0, 0: the drawing, untouched.

Frame 0: every pixel is the drawing's, unchanged.

FX-OFFSET-002: Shift 3, 0: every pixel moves exactly three pixels right, and the three columns that leave the right edge come back in at the left, so the red dot is at (2, 0) and the soft edge down column 1.

## Turbulent Displace fixtures

D-127, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/turbulent_displace/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Turbulent Displace (`core.turbulent_displace`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/turbulent_displace/media/stripes.png`: in rows 1 to 8 and columns 0 to 13, upright stripes two pixels wide, skin #f6d6be and line #1e1a24 by turns, crossed by a blue band #3a6fd8 in rows 4 and 5, touching the drawing's left edge; column 14 is the skin at half covering, its soft edge, and column 15 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. The composition frame is the effect's hidden frame: with speed not 0 the warp moves from frame to frame. With edges transparent the layer grows by the amount rounded up and the grown pixels are shown in place, as FX-TURB-017 shows. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/turbulent_displace_reference.py`**, which works D-127's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, with Fractal Noise's field F from `tools/fractal_noise_reference.py` and `tools/radial_blur_reference.py`'s bilinear rule. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/turbulent_displace/expected_turbulent_displace.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks the rule's pieces (the growth, ceil of the amount with transparent and 0 with repeat; nothing past it; the push, amount times F on channels 0 and 1), then each case's claim on its numbers: at the start each pixel reads from two to four pixels left and two to five below, not alike, the warp moves from frame to frame, and the first three columns are empty (001); amount 0 changes nothing (002); speed 0 holds the warp still (003, 004); repeat is the transparent warp wherever the sample lies inside the drawing, and reads the stripe where transparent reads emptiness (005); complexity 1 and 8 differ from 2, and 2.7 is 2 (006, 007, 014); at size 1000 every push is alike within a hundredth of a pixel (009); speed 90 meets evolution 180 at frame 2 and 360 at frame 4 (010, 011); seed 8.5 is seed 8 (012, 013); the keyed amount meets the plain amounts and the overshooting speed is held at 360 (015, 016); and moved, the warp moves with the drawing, the grown pixels show with transparent and stay empty with repeat (017, 018).

FX-TURB-001: The settings as they start: amount 10, size 60, complexity 2, evolution 0, speed 20, seed 0, edges transparent. A wave is wider than the drawing, so each pixel reads from two to four pixels left of it and two to five below, not quite alike everywhere: the drawing is carried right and up and its stripes lean and bend gently; the warp moves a little from frame 0 to 2 to 4. The first three columns read from past the drawing's left edge and are empty on every frame.

### Turbulent Displace in After Effects' units (D-328)

From P-26's tutorial 2 (Amount 80, Size 2 under a glow), approved by the owner on 2026-10-05. **Every number is produced by `tools/turbulent_ae_reference.py`**, which is `tools/turbulent_displace_reference.py`'s rule given the push `amount * min(size, 100) / 100` in place of the amount (document 21, D-328), and is in `Fixtures/turbulent_ae/expected_turbulent_ae.json`; the projects and the drawing are beside it. Each case is FX-TURB-001's composition, 16 by 10, and drawing `stripes.png`, edges transparent and unmoved unless it says. Values are linear premultiplied. Tolerance 2e-5. B-212 checks them in `verification/D-328_turbulent_ae_table.md`.

FX-TURB-AE-001: Units after_effects, amount 80, size 2, speed 0, tutorial 2's setting: the push is 80 x 2 / 100 = 1.6 pixels at most, so each pixel reads from within two pixels of itself and the stripes stay stripes, shimmering; 123 pixels are more than half covered, against the drawing's 120. Pixel (3, 4) is 0.0423114 0.158961 0.686685 1; (8, 2) is 0.716335 0.522876 0.402586 1.

FX-TURB-AE-002: The same settings in a file without units: D-127's rule as before, a push of up to 80 pixels at a wave every two, so each pixel reads from far off, mostly past the drawing: it breaks into dust, and in this small frame only 2 specks are left. Pixel (3, 4) is clear.

FX-TURB-AE-003: Units written `classic`: FX-TURB-AE-002 exactly.

FX-TURB-AE-004: Units after_effects with the settings as they start, amount 10, size 60, speed 20: the push is 6 pixels at most, D-127's amount 6 at size 60, on frames 0, 2 and 4. Frame 0 pixel (3, 4) is 0.921582 0.672443 0.514918 1.

FX-TURB-AE-005: Units after_effects, amount 3, size 1000, speed 0: past size 100 the push is the amount, so this is FX-TURB-009 exactly.

FX-TURB-AE-006: Units after_effects, amount 3, size 100, speed 0: at size 100 the push is the amount, D-127's amount 3 at size 100. Pixel (3, 4) is 0.0530255 0.110822 0.405476 1.

## Fractal Noise fixtures

D-128, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/fractal_noise/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Fractal Noise (`core.fractal_noise`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/fractal_noise/media/card.png`, Noise's card: a box of line #1e1a24 in columns 3 to 12 and rows 1 to 7, filled with skin #f6d6be, with a white patch in columns 5 and 6 and a black one in columns 9 and 10, both in rows 3 and 4, on a grey card #808080 filling rows 0 to 8; column 15 is the skin at half covering, its soft edge, and column 0 and row 9 are empty. The composition frame is the effect's hidden frame: with speed not 0 the clouds change from frame to frame. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/fractal_noise_reference.py`**, which works D-128's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, with the noise field V and F it holds for Fractal Noise and Turbulent Displace alike and Noise's hash from `tools/noise_reference.py`. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/fractal_noise/expected_fractal_noise.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks the field's pieces (the fade's ends and middle, V equal to the corner's hash on a lattice corner, negative corners included, V continuous across a cell, one octave of F equal to V, F inside -1..1, the two channels different), then each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering and leaves the empty pixels empty (all); black to white at normal 100 paints each shown pixel a grey, the value v, and at the start the greys are close and speed 0 holds frame 4 at frame 0 (001); size 4 varies more (002); complexity 1.9 is the one octave, V itself (003); contrast 0 is exactly the middle, contrast 300 three times as far from it and brightness 30 lifted by 0.3, both held at black and white, and brightness -100 all black (005 to 008); speed 90 meets evolution 180 at frame 2 and 360 at frame 4, and the keyed evolution meets them at its frames (009 to 011); seed 7.9 is seed 7 (012, 013); the two colours mix in encoded values and capitals change nothing (014, 015); multiply only darkens and keeps black, screen only lightens and keeps white, add is not held (016 to 018); the overshooting opacity is held at 100 (019); and moved, the clouds move with the drawing (020).

### D-318: complexity to 20, brightness from -200 to 200

D-318, from the owner's approval of D-308 on 2026-10-04. **Every number is produced by `tools/fractal_noise_d318_reference.py`**, which is `tools/fractal_noise_reference.py`'s field and rule with the wider ranges, and is in `Fixtures/fractal_noise/expected_fractal_noise_d318.json`; the projects are `fx_fractal_029.json` to `fx_fractal_033.json`, on the same card. Tolerance 2e-5. The reference checks that twenty octaves differ from eight by less than 0.05 anywhere (each octave is half the last), that brightness 200 is the light colour everywhere the card shows, and that FX-FRACTAL-030 leaves most of the card at the dark colour but not all of it.

## Light Wrap fixtures

D-132, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/light_wrap/`, holding two drawings the same size, unmoved unless the case says: `Fixtures/light_wrap/media/bands.png` at the bottom, opaque bands of colour four columns wide, yellow #ffd23c, cyan #3cc8ff, pink #ff50c8 and green #8cff5a from the left, and above it `Fixtures/light_wrap/media/box.png` with one Light Wrap (`core.light_wrap`) on it: a box of line #1e1a24 in columns 5 to 10 and rows 2 to 7, filled with skin #f6d6be, with the line at half covering down column 4, rows 3 to 6, as its antialiased edge; everything else in the box drawing is empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values of the whole frame, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the frame the same composition draws with its Light Wrap taken out, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/light_wrap_reference.py`**, which works D-132's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawings' 8-bit values, blurring with `tools/edges_reference.py`'s two-dimensional Gaussian summed directly, and composes the layers by document 21's over and multiply. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/light_wrap/expected_light_wrap.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: the wrap never changes a covering, only brightens, and leaves every pixel the box does not cover as it would be without it (all); every pixel of the box takes light, its corner more than its middle, and screen stays within the covering (001); at width 3 the corner takes more than twenty times the middle's light (002); at width 20 less light arrives everywhere, almost evenly (003); intensity 400 is at least as bright as 100 (004); intensity 0, nothing beneath, an adjustment layer and a switched-off wrap change nothing (005, 008, 015, 016); width 0 lights only the half-covered edge, by the rule worked by hand (006); add is at least as bright as screen and may pass the covering (007); with the bands moved the far edge takes less (009); moved, the box takes the light behind its new place (010); opacity and multiply apply to the wrapped box (011, 012); an Exposure anywhere in the stack runs before the wrap (013, 014); and the keyed width and intensity meet the plain cases at their frames (017, 018).

FX-WRAP-001: The defaults, width 10, intensity 100, screen, on the box over the bands: every pixel of the box takes the bands' light, blurred at sigma 3.33, most at its edges and least in its middle, each colour from the bands nearest it; its covering is unchanged, and the bands around it are untouched.

## Invert fixtures

D-134, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/invert/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Invert (`core.invert`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/invert/media/bands.png`: bands of colour, two columns each, in rows 1 to 8, black #000000 in columns 1 and 2, the line #1e1a24 in 3 and 4, a red trace #c82828 in 5 and 6, a grey #808080 in 7 and 8, skin #f6d6be in 9 and 10, a blue #3a6fd8 in 11 and 12 and white #ffffff in 13 and 14, with the skin at half covering in column 15 of rows 1 to 4 and at a quarter covering in rows 5 to 8, a soft edge; column 0 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. Inverted, each 8-bit channel v becomes 255 - v, so every band turns a colour the owner can name. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/invert_reference.py`**, which works D-134's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/invert/expected_invert.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every colour choice keeps every pixel's covering and leaves the empty pixels empty (all but the alpha cases); rgb at 100 turns each 8-bit channel v into 255 - v, black to white and white to black (001); amount 0 changes nothing, for a colour choice or for alpha (002, 013); amount 50 turns every shown pixel the same mid grey at its own covering (003), and 25 halves every colour's contrast about the middle (004); red, green or blue alone turns that channel as rgb does and keeps the other two exactly, and the three in turn make rgb (005 to 007); alpha at 100 makes what fully showed disappear, turns the empty pixels opaque black and gives the soft edge the opposite covering in its own colour (008), and at 50 gives every pixel half covering in its own colour (009); the keyed amounts meet the plain cases at their frames, an overshooting ease held at 100 (010 to 012); and moved, the effect moves with the drawing, the columns outside the layer staying empty even for alpha (014, 015).

FX-INVERT-001: Channel rgb, amount 100, the settings as they start: every colour that shows turns to its opposite, each 8-bit channel v becoming 255 - v: black turns white and white black, the line #1e1a24 a pale #e1e5db, the red #c82828 a cyan #37d7d7, the grey #808080 a hair darker, #7f7f7f, the skin #f6d6be a deep #092941 and the blue #3a6fd8 an ochre #c59027; the soft edge turns #092941 at its own covering, and the empty pixels stay empty.

## Brightness & Contrast fixtures

D-135, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/brightness_contrast/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Brightness & Contrast (`core.brightness_contrast`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/brightness_contrast/media/tones.png`: in rows 1 to 8, one column each, black #000000 in column 1, the line #1e1a24 in 2, a dark grey #404040 in 3, a grey #808080 in 4 (a hair above half), a light grey #c0c0c0 in 5, skin #f6d6be in 6, white #ffffff in 7, the shaded skin #dca08c in 8, a blue #3a6fd8 in 9, a red #d6283c in 10 and a pink #f09696 in 11, with the skin at half covering in column 12 and the blue at a quarter covering in column 13 as soft edges; columns 0, 14 and 15 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/brightness_contrast_reference.py`**, which works D-135's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/brightness_contrast/expected_brightness_contrast.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering, leaves the empty pixels empty, and adjusts the soft edges as the skin and the blue at their own covering (all); both at 0 change nothing (001, 013 frame 2); brightness adds its levels of 255 to every channel, held at full and at 0, black lifted to #323232 and #969696 and white lowered to #cdcdcd and #696969 (002 to 005); contrast 50 pushes the tones apart and leaves black and white as they are (006), -50 draws them half way to the middle (007), -100 turns every shown pixel flat mid grey (008) and 100 turns every channel black or full but the grey's, at 0.696 (009); contrast works before brightness (010, 011); the keyed, eased and held settings meet the plain cases at their frames, an overshooting ease held at 150 (012 to 015); and moved, the effect moves with the drawing (016).

FX-BRICON-001: Brightness 0 and contrast 0, the settings as they start: the drawing, untouched.

Frame 0: every pixel is the drawing's, unchanged.

FX-BRICON-002: Brightness 50: every channel of every shown pixel is lifted 50 levels of 255 as it is written: black turns #323232, the grey #b2b2b2; the white, already full, is held there and stays white, and the skin's red and green are held at full while its blue rises to 240.

## Black & White fixtures

D-136, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/black_white/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Black & White (`core.black_white`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/black_white/media/swatches.png`, swatches one column wide. In rows 1 to 4: the six pure colours red #ff0000, yellow #ffff00, green #00ff00, cyan #00ffff, blue #0000ff and magenta #ff00ff in columns 1 to 6, grey #808080, white #ffffff and black #000000 in columns 7 to 9, and the red at half covering in column 10 as a soft edge. In rows 5 to 8: one colour for each order of the three channels, skin #f6d6be (red, green, blue), pink #ff4080 (red, blue, green), leaf #80c040 (green, red, blue), teal #20c080 (green, blue, red), the line #1e1a24 (blue, red, green) and sky #4080c0 (blue, green, red) in columns 1 to 6, the trace red #c82828 in column 7, the skin's shadow #dca08c in column 8 and the skin at half covering in column 9. Column 0, rows 0 and 9 and everything to the swatches' right are empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/black_white_reference.py`**, which works D-136's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/black_white/expected_black_white.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers, and the rule's pieces: ties are ordered red, green, blue, and a colour a hair either side of a tie gives the same grey, so the rule has no cliff; each pure colour gives its own number over 100; a grey gives itself whatever the numbers; all six at 100 give the largest channel and all at 0 the smallest (002, 003). Every case keeps every pixel's covering, leaves the empty pixels empty, turns every pixel that shows grey, leaves grey, white and black exactly as drawn, and makes each half-covered pixel the full one's grey at half covering (all); the start settings give the worked greys (001); each of the six numbers changes only the colours it weights, lifting to white or holding at black at its ends (004 to 010); a red filter lightens the warm colours and darkens the cool ones, holding blue and cyan at black (011); the keyed numbers meet the plain cases at their frames, an overshooting ease held at 300 or -200 (012 to 015); and moved, the effect moves with the drawing (016).

FX-BW-001: The settings as they start, 40, 60, 40, 60, 20, 80: every pixel that shows turns grey. Each pure colour becomes the grey of its own number: red and green #666666 (102), yellow and cyan #999999 (153), blue #333333 (51), magenta #cccccc (204). Grey, white and black stay exactly as they are. The skin becomes 217.2 on the 8-bit scale, the pink 166, the leaf 128, the teal and the sky 115.2, the line 30.4, the trace red 104 and the shadow 176; the half-covered red and skin are the red's and the skin's greys at half covering.

## Posterize fixtures

D-137, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/posterize/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Posterize (`core.posterize`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/posterize/media/ramps.png`, four bands of two rows each in columns 1 to 14: rows 1 and 2 a grey ramp, 0, 20, 42, 43, 64, 85, 100, 127, 128, 150, 170, 212, 213 and 255 (either side of levels 6's steps at 42.5, 127.5 and 212.5, and on its steps at 85 and 170); rows 3 and 4 a warm-to-cool ramp, red rising 0, 20, 39, 59, 78, 98, 118, 137, 157, 177, 196, 216, 235, 255 as blue falls from 255 to 0, green 96; rows 5 and 6 swatches, line #1e1a24 in columns 1 and 2, skin #f6d6be in 3 to 5, shadow #dca08c in 6 to 8, red #c82828 in 9 and 10, blue #4060ff in 11 and 12, white in 13 and black in 14; rows 7 and 8 a skin shading from the shadow #dca08c at column 1 to the skin #f6d6be at column 14. Column 15 holds each band's soft edge at half covering: the grey 128, the ramp's last colour #ff6000, the skin and the line. Column 0 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/posterize_reference.py`**, which works D-137's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/posterize/expected_posterize.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. The rule is a cliff, and the tool asserts that no channel any case decides lies within 1e-5 of a step once the rule's 1e-4 is added, so the build's single precision decides every pixel the same way.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering, leaves the empty pixels empty, and gives each half-covering pixel the same steps as its colour at full covering (all); at the start every channel lands on one of six steps, the greys either side of a step a whole step apart, black and white kept, the grey ramp six flat greys (001); levels 2 gives at most eight colours, the grey 127 black and 128 white (002); at levels 3 the greys on a step are taken up by the 1e-4 (003); at 16 every channel is within one step of its own (004); 256 changes nothing (005) and 255 lifts every channel but black and white by at most one 8-bit step (006); 6.9 counts as 6 (007); the keyed levels meet the plain cases at their frames, their fractions dropped (008, 009), an overshooting ease is held at 2 (010) and a hold key holds (011); and moved, the steps move with the drawing (012).

FX-POSTER-001: Levels 6, as it starts: every channel of every pixel that shows lands on one of six steps, 0, 51, 102, 153, 204 or 255 (encoded, of 255); the grey ramp turns to six flat greys, the greys 42 and 43 either side of a step landing on 0 and 51, 127 and 128 on 102 and 153, 212 and 213 on 204 and 255; black and white stay; a pixel at half covering takes the same steps as its colour at full covering, at its own covering; the empty pixels stay empty.

## Threshold fixtures

D-138, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/threshold/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Threshold (`core.threshold`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/threshold/media/tones.png`, bands of colour one column wide in rows 1 to 8, ordered by their encoded luma times 255: black 0 (column 1), blue #0000ff 18.411 (2), the line #1e1a24 27.5724 (3), red #ff0000 54.213 (4), dark grey #404040 64 (5), grey #7f7f7f 127 (6), grey #808080 128 (7), the shadow skin #dca08c 171.312 (8), green #00ff00 182.376 (9), light grey #c0c0c0 192 (10), the skin #f6d6be 219.0704 (11) and white 255 (12), then the skin at half covering (13) and the line at half covering (14); columns 0 and 15 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/threshold_reference.py`**, which works D-138's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/threshold/expected_threshold.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering, leaves the empty pixels empty, turns every shown pixel pure white or pure black at its own covering, the soft edges as their solid colours, and decides no pixel within 1e-5 of the level, the cliff (all); a grey exactly on the level turns white (001, 006, 007) and a level between two steps turns it black (008); level 0 whitens everything and 255 keeps only white (002, 003); blue counts darker than the line, and red brighter (004, 005); the shadow skin splits from the lit skin (009) and pure green from the light grey (010); the keyed, held and overshooting levels meet the plain cases at their frames, black spreading from the darkest up (011, 012, 013); and moved, the result moves with the drawing (014).

FX-THRESH-001: Level 128, the setting as it starts: black, blue, the line, red, the dark grey and grey 127 turn black; grey 128, exactly on the level, turns white, as do the shadow skin, green, the light grey, the skin and white; the soft skin turns white and the soft line black, each at its own half covering.
