## Channel Mixer fixtures

D-139, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/channel_mixer/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Channel Mixer (`core.channel_mixer`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/channel_mixer/media/swatches.png`: a box of line #1e1a24 in columns 2 to 14 and rows 1 to 8 holding, in rows 2 to 7, skin #f6d6be in columns 3 and 4, a red #c82828 in 5 and 6, a green #3cb450 in 7 and 8, a blue #4060ff in 9 and 10, white in 11, a grey #808080 in 12 and black in 13; down its left side, column 1, the line at half covering in rows 1 to 4 and the skin at half covering in rows 5 to 8, as soft edges. Column 0, column 15 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. A row's four numbers are written red, green, blue and constant. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/channel_mixer_reference.py`**, which works D-139's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/channel_mixer/expected_channel_mixer.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers, each named swatch against its exact 8-bit result: every case keeps every pixel's covering, leaves the empty pixels empty, and mixes each soft edge as its colour at full covering (all); the rows as they start change nothing (001, 012 frame 0, 013 frame 0, 014 frame 2); swapping red and blue, or green from red, leaves every grey alone (002, 010, 012 frame 2); a row of 0 takes its channel away (003); 200 doubles a channel, held at the top (004, 014 frame 4); a constant lifts a channel half the scale at 50 (005); the negative turns white black and black white (006); monochrome takes the red row for every channel and ignores the other two (007 to 009, 015); the ends of the range are held inside the scale (011); the keyed rows meet the plain cases at their frames, an overshooting ease held at 200 (012 to 015); and moved, the effect moves with the drawing (016).

FX-MIXER-001: The settings as they start, red 100, 0, 0, 0, green 0, 100, 0, 0, blue 0, 0, 100, 0, monochrome off: the drawing, untouched.

Frame 0: every pixel is the drawing's, unchanged.

## Vibrance fixtures

D-140, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/vibrance/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Vibrance (`core.vibrance`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/vibrance/media/colours.png`: bands of colour from the dullest to the most vivid, two columns each, in rows 1 to 8, a grey #808080 in columns 1 and 2 (no colour at all, s = 0), the line #1e1a24 in 3 and 4 (s = 0.04), a dull tan #a08c78 in 5 and 6 (s = 0.16), skin #f6d6be in 7 and 8 (s = 0.22), the ball's blue #3a6fd8 in 9 and 10 (s = 0.62), a red trace #c82828 in 11 and 12 (s = 0.63) and pure red #ff0000 in 13 and 14 (s = 1), with the skin at half covering in column 15 as a soft edge; column 0 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. Here s is a colour's spread, its largest encoded channel less its smallest: vibrance pushes a colour 1 + vibrance / 100 (1 - s) times as far from its own grey, so the grey, having no colour, never moves, and the pure red is left alone by vibrance and moved by saturation only. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own (the pure red under vibrance -100 comes back within one rounding step, 6e-16, and is not listed).

**Every number below is produced by `tools/vibrance_reference.py`**, which works D-140's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/vibrance/expected_vibrance.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering, leaves the empty pixels empty, never moves the grey, and grades the soft edge as the skin at half covering (all); both at 0 change nothing (001, 011 frame 2); each colour is its own colour pushed exactly 1 + saturation / 100 + vibrance / 100 (1 - s) times from its grey, each channel held between 0 and 1, with the channels that pass an end named in the claim (002 to 009); vibrance 100 moves the dull tan 1.84 times and the vivid blue 1.38 and leaves the pure red exactly as it is (002); vibrance -100 leaves each colour s of itself and the pure red all of it (003); saturation 100 doubles every colour alike (004); saturation -100 makes every colour its own grey, the pure red #363636 but for rounding (005); vibrance and saturation against each other keep the dull colours and fade the vivid (006, 007), or the other way round (008); an everyday grade pushes the pure red past both its ends and so leaves it pure red (009); the keyed numbers meet the plain cases at their frames, an overshooting ease held at -100 (010 to 012); and moved, the effect moves with the drawing (013).

## Leave Color fixtures

D-141, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/leave_color/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Leave Color (`core.leave_color`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/leave_color/media/swatches.png`: a box of line #1e1a24 in columns 2 to 14 and rows 1 to 8 holding, in rows 2 to 7, one column each of red #c82828 (column 3), pink #ff0040 (4), the skin's shadow #dca08c (5), skin #f6d6be (6), orange #ff9900 (7), yellow #ffff00 (8), green #40c040 (9), teal #40c0c0 (10), blue #4060ff (11), violet #9040c0 (12) and magenta #ff00ff (13); down its left side, column 1, the red at half covering in rows 1 to 4 and the blue at half covering in rows 5 to 8; column 0, column 15 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. Their hues, in degrees, are 0 (red), 344.94 (pink), 15 (shadow), 25.71 (skin), 36 (orange), 60 (yellow), 120 (green), 180 (teal), 229.95 (blue), 277.5 (violet), 300 (magenta) and 264 (line). Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/leave_color_reference.py`**, which works D-141's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, with colour key's hue (D-97). The same numbers are in `Fixtures/leave_color/expected_leave_color.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering and leaves the empty pixels empty, and a pixel at half covering takes the colour of its colour at full covering (all); at softness 0 no pixel's hue distance lies within 1e-5 of the tolerance, the cliff (004 to 006); the start settings keep the reds, the shadow and the skin exactly, half drain the orange and turn the rest fully grey, each to its own brightness (001); amount 0 and tolerance 100 change nothing (002, 012) and amount 50 goes half way (003); a narrow hard edge keeps only the red (004) and a wide one the warm half of the wheel (005); softness 0 drops the orange and a wide softness keeps part of the yellow and the magenta, alike, across the wheel's seam (006, 007); a blue colour keeps the blue and part of the line (008), a grey colour keeps nothing (009), capitals change nothing (010), and an orange colour keeps the skin tones (011); the keyed tolerance and amount meet the plain cases at their frames, and an overshooting ease is held at 100 (013 to 015); and moved, the effect moves with the drawing (016).

FX-LEAVE-001: The settings as they start: #ff0000, tolerance 15, softness 10, amount 100. The red, the pink across the wheel's seam (15 degrees the other way), the skin's shadow and the skin, all within 27 degrees of red, are kept exactly; the orange, 36 degrees off, half way across the soft band, is half drained; the yellow, green, teal, blue, violet, magenta and the line turn fully grey, each to its own brightness. The red at half covering is kept; the blue at half covering turns the same grey as the blue, at its own covering; the empty pixels stay empty.

## Solarize fixtures

D-142, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/solarize/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Solarize (`core.solarize`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/solarize/media/bands.png`: one column each of colour in rows 1 to 8, black #000000 in column 1, the line #1e1a24 in 2, a dark grey #404040 in 3, #7f7f7f in 4, a grey #808080 in 5, a light grey #c0c0c0 in 6, skin #f6d6be in 7, a red trace #c82828 in 8, a night blue #3a5a9a in 9 and white #ffffff in 10, with the skin at half covering in column 11 and the grey at half covering in column 12 as soft edges; columns 0 and 13 to 15 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. The grey #808080 sits exactly on the starting threshold, 128, and #7f7f7f one below it, so the two side by side show the cliff. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/solarize_reference.py`**, which works D-142's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/solarize/expected_solarize.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering, leaves the empty pixels empty, and turns the soft edges as the skin and the grey at half covering (all); no channel any case decides sits within 1e-5 of the threshold, the nearest being an 8-bit value exactly on it, 1e-4 away (all); at 128 a channel on the threshold is turned over and one below is kept, each channel on its own (001); at 0 everything is inverted (002), at 255 only full channels (003), and at 1 everything but a channel at 0 (004); an 8-bit value on the threshold is inverted at 64 and 200 (005, 007) and kept once the threshold is one above it (006); a threshold between two 8-bit values acts as the next whole number (008); the keyed thresholds, linear, held and overshooting, meet the plain cases at their frames, the overshoot held at 255 (009 to 011); and moved, the effect moves with the drawing (012).

FX-SOLAR-001: Threshold 128, as it starts: every channel at 128 or above is turned over. The grey #808080, on the threshold, turns #7f7f7f, while #7f7f7f beside it, one below, stays; the light grey turns #3f3f3f and the white black; the skin turns a deep blue #092941 (red, green and blue all above 128); the red trace keeps its green and blue and its red falls to 55; the night blue keeps its red and green and its blue falls to 101; black, the line and the dark grey, all below, stay as they are.

## Mosaic fixtures

D-144, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/mosaic/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Mosaic (`core.mosaic`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/mosaic/media/strip.png`: in columns 4 to 11, skin #f6d6be in rows 0 to 3, shadow #dca08c in rows 4 and 5 and a line #1e1a24 along row 6; white #ffffff in rows 7 to 9 from column 4 to the right edge; the skin at half covering down column 3, rows 0 to 6, a soft edge; one red dot #c82828 at (13, 5); and everything else empty, so most blocks mix colours with empty pixels. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/mosaic_reference.py`**, which works D-144's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, and, for FX-MOSAIC-013, `tools/directional_blur_reference.py`'s blur ahead of it. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/mosaic/expected_mosaic.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. Which block a pixel falls in is a choice made from a number: the tool checks that every case's size is held exactly by single precision and that no pixel lies within 1e-5 of a block's edge unless exactly on it, where the division is exact in both precisions (the closest off an edge is 0.001).

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every value stays within its covering, and with nothing moved or grown each channel's total over the frame is the drawing's (all); as it starts, two blocks across, the right one cut short to six columns, each flat at the mean of its pixels, 63.5 and 33 pixels' worth of covering (001); size 1 changes nothing (002); sizes 2, 4, 3, 2.5, 8 and 10.5 give their blocks, cut short at the right and bottom edges, a block all of skin staying skin, an empty block staying empty, and the corner pixel a block of its own at size 3 (003 to 006, 009, 014); sizes 16 and 1000 make one block, the drawing's mean (007, 008); the keyed size and the overshooting ease held at 1000 meet the plain cases at their frames (010, 011); moved, the blocks move with the drawing (012); and after a directional blur that grew the layer the blocks are still laid from the drawing's own corner, the bottom row of blocks taking in the grown empty rows below the frame (013).

FX-MOSAIC-001: The settings as they start, size 10: two blocks across, columns 0 to 9 and a block cut short at the right edge, columns 10 to 15, each the full height and one flat colour, the mean of its pixels; both are partly empty, so both come out partly covered, the left 63.5 of its 100 pixels' worth, the right 33 of its 60, and the frame keeps each channel's total.

## Emboss fixtures

D-145, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/emboss/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Emboss (`core.emboss`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/emboss/media/plate.png`: in rows 1 to 8, columns 0 to 13, skin #f6d6be (picture luma 0.8619), crossed by the ball's blue band #3a6fd8 (0.4520) in rows 4 and 5, with a dark square of the line colour #1e1a24 (0.1087) in columns 6 to 9, rows 2 to 7, over the band; the skin and the band touch the drawing's left edge, so a look past it is held at the first column. Column 14 is the skin at half covering (0.6330, its colour over black), a soft edge; column 15 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. Each pixel that shows looks `relief` pixels ahead along the direction and as far behind, and v = 0.5 + (luma ahead - luma behind) contrast / 100 is its grey as written. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own (under relief 0 in color mode every pixel comes back within one rounding step, 2e-16, and is not listed).

**Every number below is produced by `tools/emboss_reference.py`**, which works D-145's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/emboss/expected_emboss.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering and leaves the empty pixels empty (all); each grey-mode pixel is one grey, v held between 0 and 1, worked from its two held bilinear looks (001, 006 to 012); a look past the drawing's left edge reads its first column, not emptiness (006, 012); the flat parts are the middle grey, the drawing stands up from the emptiness and the band and dark square sink in, each named edge dark or light as claimed (001); relief 0 and contrast 0 give flat grey, and relief 0 in color mode the drawing (002 to 004); color mode moves each channel as written by v - 0.5 and keeps the flat parts' colours (005); a level or upright direction reads exactly the neighbouring pixels, and the opposite direction gives 1 less the grey (006 to 008); contrast 300 and 1000 multiply each difference, 88 edge pixels held at black or white under 1000 and 8 faint ones not (009, 010); relief 2.5 leaves one pixel flat (011); relief 100 holds both looks at the drawing's edges, one grey per row (012); the keyed numbers meet the plain cases at their frames, an overshooting ease held at 1000 (013 to 015); a direction a whole turn away is the same (016, 017); and moved, the effect moves with the drawing and nothing grows (018).

FX-EMBOSS-001: The settings as they start: direction 135, relief 1, contrast 100, mode grey. Every pixel that shows turns a grey, lighter where the picture ahead of it (down and to the right) is brighter than behind it and darker where it is darker: the flat skin and the middle of the square stay a middle grey (0.5 as written). The drawing, brighter than the emptiness around it, stands up: its top row is light, and its bottom row and its soft right-hand column dark. The dark square and the band sink in: their top edges go dark and their bottom edges light, and the square's left edge dark and its right edge light. The soft column is grey at its half covering; the empty pixels stay empty.

## Find Edges fixtures

D-146, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/find_edges/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Find Edges (`core.find_edges`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/find_edges/media/bands.png`: in rows 1 to 8, skin #f6d6be in columns 1 to 5, the line #1e1a24 one pixel wide in column 6, skin in columns 7 to 9 of rows 1 to 4 over its shade #dca08c in rows 5 to 8, a red trace #c82828 in column 10, a blue #3a6fd8 in columns 11 to 13, white #ffffff in column 14, and in column 15 the skin at half covering in rows 1 to 4 and at a quarter covering in rows 5 to 8, a soft edge; column 0 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. So the cases show flat colour (which turns white), a line, a boundary between two colours, a soft one (the skin and its shade), a faint one (the blue beside the red), and the drawing's own outline against transparency. FX-FINDEDGES-011 and 012 use `Fixtures/find_edges/media/card.png`, a flat skin card filling the drawing. The prefix is FX-FINDEDGES, not FX-EDGES, which D-109's Repeat Edge Pixels fixtures already use. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/find_edges_reference.py`**, which works D-146's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/find_edges/expected_find_edges.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers, and the rule's pieces worked by hand from the 8-bit values: the picture luma is the colour over black, 0 for an empty pixel and darker for the soft edge; the skin over its shade gives m = 2 (y(skin) - y(shade)), about 0.36, below the hold at 1. Every case keeps every pixel's covering and leaves the empty pixels empty. At 100 every shown pixel turns a grey, 1 - m: the flat skin and blue white, the outline against the empty rows and column black, the one-pixel line black either side and white in its own middle where the skin either side matches, the blue beside the red trace barely darker (001); amount 0 changes nothing, invert off or on (002, 010); invert on is 1 minus the same grey (003); 50 and 25 go half and a quarter of the way from each pixel's colour to that grey (004 to 006); the keyed amounts meet the plain cases at their frames, an overshooting ease held at 100 (007 to 009); a flat card that fills the drawing has no edge at its border, as the border repeats: all white, or with invert on all black (011, 012); and moved, the effect moves with the drawing, the columns outside the layer staying empty (013, 014).

FX-FINDEDGES-001: Invert off, amount 100, the settings as they start: dark lines on white. Where the picture is flat, inside the skin and the blue, the pixel turns pure white; the drawing's own outline against the empty rows and column turns black; the line, one pixel wide in column 6, comes out as two black lines either side of it, its own middle white in rows 2 and 3, where the skin either side matches (the rule looks at a pixel's neighbours, not the pixel), and grey lower down, where the shade begins on one side; the skin meets its shade in a grey edge; the blue beside the red trace barely darkens; every shown pixel turns a grey, at its own covering, the soft edge keeping its covering, and the empty pixels stay empty.

## Sharpen fixtures

D-147, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/sharpen/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Sharpen (`core.sharpen`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/sharpen/media/picture.png`: rows 0 and 9 are empty; on the left a patch of skin #f6d6be in columns 0 to 2 with the skin at half covering in column 3 as its soft edge, alone, with nothing of another colour within three pixels; columns 4 to 6 empty; the line #1e1a24 at half covering down column 7, rows 3 to 6; and in columns 8 to 15 a box of line round skin, with the ball's blue #3a6fd8 as a band across rows 4 and 5. Sharpen pushes each colour away from the blurred colour around it, the blur's colour divided by its own covering, so a flat colour is left alone however much of its blur is empty: the patch's outline against the empty pixels is not an edge, and at the starting radius the patch is left as it is. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own (a flat colour comes back within a rounding step, under 1e-12, and is not listed).

**Every number below is produced by `tools/sharpen_reference.py`**, which works D-147's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, blurring with document 21's Gaussian summed directly and cut back to the drawing's own size. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/sharpen/expected_sharpen.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering, leaves the empty pixels empty and keeps every channel within its covering (all); a flat colour, whole or at half covering beside empty pixels, is left as it is, and amount 0 or radius 0 leave the input exactly (the rule's pieces, 002, 003); at the start settings exactly the box and the soft line change, the line goes to black, the skin beside it grows lighter with its red held at 1, the skin beside the band loses blue while the band gains it, and the patch is left as it is (001); amount 50 pushes each colour exactly half as far and amount 500 exactly five times as far wherever nothing is held at 0 or 1, and never less far or the other way (004, 005); at 500 the skin along the line is white, the skin beside the band pale yellow and the band pure blue (005); radius 0.5 still leaves the patch alone (006), while radius 3 lightens every pixel of it, its soft edge most (007); the keyed numbers meet the plain cases at their frames, an overshooting ease held at 500 (008 to 010); moved, the effect moves with the drawing (011); and amount 250 at radius 1.5 pushes the box further than 001 and reaches only the patch's right two columns, faintly (012).

FX-SHARPEN-001: Amount 100 and radius 1, the settings as they start: each colour is pushed away from the blurred colour around it, so the two sides of every edge inside the box move apart. The line, dark beside the skin, is pushed to black all round the box and down the soft column 7; the skin beside the line grows lighter, its red held at 1; the skin beside the band loses blue, and the band loses red and green and gains blue. Every pixel of the box and of the soft line changes; the patch of skin on the left, with its soft edge, has no other colour within reach of the blur and is left as it is but for rounding, as its outline against the empty pixels is not an edge. Every covering is kept, and the empty pixels stay empty.

## Diffusion fixtures

D-148, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/diffusion/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Diffusion (`core.diffusion`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/diffusion/media/cel.png`, a small cel in rows 1 to 8: a deep shadow #281e3c in columns 1 to 6 holding the ball's highlight #fff5ea in columns 3 and 4, rows 3 to 5; the line #1e1a24 down column 7; skin #f6d6be in columns 8 to 11 with a hole at (10, 6); the ball's blue #3a6fd8 in columns 12 to 14; and the skin at half covering down column 15, a soft edge with nothing to its right. Column 0 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. The glow is the drawing through document 21's Gaussian blur at sigma radius / 3, read at the drawing's own pixels and divided by its own covering, so the emptiness round the cel does not darken it. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/diffusion_reference.py`**, which works D-148's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, summing the blur's two-dimensional kernel directly. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/diffusion/expected_diffusion.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel's covering and leaves the empty pixels, the hole among them, empty, and screen and lighten never darken a channel (all); the defaults change every pixel that shows and lift every pixel of the shadow and the line more than any of the skin or the light, whose full red stays at 1, one pixel worked by hand (001); amount 50 is exactly halfway between the drawing and amount 100 (002, and 009 against 008); amount 0 and radius 0 change nothing (003, 004); a tight glow lifts the shadow next to the light more and the far corner less than a fifth as much (005), and a wide one lifts the shadow nearly evenly, within 1.3 times, where radius 10 varies by more than twice (006); lighten takes each channel's larger and leaves the light exactly as it is (007); normal at 100 makes every pixel the glow's own colour, the soft edge's more than twice its blur's darkened value (008); the keyed numbers meet the plain cases at their frames, an overshooting ease held at 100 (010, 011); and moved, the effect moves with the drawing (012). A picture of one colour with edges against nothing is checked to come back from normal at 100 as it went in.

FX-DIFFUSE-001: The settings as they start, radius 10, amount 50, screen: every pixel that shows is lightened, never darkened, by half its screen with the glow; every pixel of the dark shadow and the line lifts more than any of the pale skin or the light, whose red, already full, stays at 1; the coverings are kept, and the empty pixels, the hole in the skin among them, stay empty.

### Diffusion's second pass (D-364)

Diffusion's second pass (D-364, B-243): the same glow laid on again over the first pass in soft light or overlay, as the layer modes lay it (D-301), by `second_amount` per cent; at 0 the effect is D-148's exactly. Every case is a project like those above, the same cel, 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames, with `second_amount` and `second_blend` written in the effect's parameters. **Every number is produced by `tools/diffusion_second_reference.py`**, which reuses `tools/diffusion_reference.py` for the drawing, blur and first pass and works the second pass from the W3C's overlay and soft light, and is in `Fixtures/diffusion/expected_diffusion_second.json`, the projects beside it. Tolerance 2e-5.

FX-DIFFUSE-019 (`fx_diffuse_019.json`): The two-layer diffusion as tomoex lays it: radius 10, lighten at 50, then soft light at 50. The shadow and the line lift as in lighten alone, then the soft light deepens the contrast a little: every dark channel (encoded below a half) of the glow pulls its pixel down, every light one lifts it. Frames 0.

FX-DIFFUSE-020 (`fx_diffuse_020.json`): Screen at 50 then soft light at 50: the settings as they start (FX-DIFFUSE-001) with the second pass laid on. Frames 0.

FX-DIFFUSE-021 (`fx_diffuse_021.json`): Lighten at 50 then overlay at 30. Frames 0.

FX-DIFFUSE-022 (`fx_diffuse_022.json`): Screen at 50 with the second pass written at 0: exactly FX-DIFFUSE-001, sample for sample. Frames 0.

FX-DIFFUSE-023 (`fx_diffuse_023.json`): Radius 3, amount 0, soft light at 100: only the second pass, the blurred picture in soft light over the drawing. Each channel moves toward the glow's side of an encoded half, darker where the glow is dark, lighter where it is light: the shadow's far corner (1, 1) darkens in every channel, and every skin pixel lightens in every channel. Frames 0.

FX-DIFFUSE-024 (`fx_diffuse_024.json`): Radius 3, amount 0, overlay at 100: only the second pass, in overlay; the same directions as FX-DIFFUSE-023. Frames 0.

FX-DIFFUSE-025 (`fx_diffuse_025.json`): Radius 0 with the second pass at 50: the drawing, untouched. Frames 0.

FX-DIFFUSE-026 (`fx_diffuse_026.json`): Second amount keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 100 at frame 4, linear, over lighten at 50: frame 0 is lighten alone, frame 2 is FX-DIFFUSE-019, frame 4 the soft light laid fully on. Frames 0, 2, 4.

FX-DIFFUSE-027 (`fx_diffuse_027.json`): Second amount keyed from 0 to 100, eased past its end: held at 100 from frame 2, so frames 2 and 4 are FX-DIFFUSE-026's frame 4. Frames 0, 2, 4.

FX-DIFFUSE-028 (`fx_diffuse_028.json`): FX-DIFFUSE-019 moved three pixels right: the same, moved. Frames 0, 3.

FX-DIFFUSE-029 (`fx_diffuse_029.json`): Second amount 101, above 100. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning. Warning `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`. Frames 0, 4.

FX-DIFFUSE-030 (`fx_diffuse_030.json`): Second amount -1, below 0. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning. Warning `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`. Frames 0, 4.

## Wave Warp fixtures

D-149, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/wave_warp/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Wave Warp (`core.wave_warp`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/wave_warp/media/stripes.png`: in rows 0 to 8 and columns 0 to 13, upright stripes two pixels wide, skin #f6d6be and line #1e1a24 by turns starting with skin, crossed by a blue band #3a6fd8 in rows 4 and 5, touching the drawing's top and left edges; column 14 is the skin at half covering, a soft edge; column 15 and row 9 are empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly. A layer that grows is shown with its grown pixels in place, so in the moved cases the columns left of the drawing are the grown pixels.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/wave_warp_reference.py`**, which works D-149's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, sampling by `tools/radial_blur_reference.py`'s bilinear rule, held for repeat. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/wave_warp/expected_wave_warp.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel premultiplied with its covering in 0..1 (all); as it starts, each column is pushed down by 10 sin(2 pi X / 40), columns 7 to 12 by more than 9, so their rows 0 to 8 are empty (001); height 0 changes nothing (002); at height 2 and width 8 the band is carried down into rows 6 and 7 in columns 1 and 2 and up into rows 2 and 3 in columns 5 and 6, and the pushed-down columns lose covering at the top (003); the triangle never pushes further than the sine (004); direction 0 pushes along the rows, leaving the band blue from column 3 to 11 (005); direction 45 differs from both (006); direction 450 is 003 exactly and direction 270 at phase 0 is 003 (007, 008); phase 90 raises the band two pixels sooner (009), and speed 45 meets 003, phase 90 and phase 180 at frames 0, 2 and 4, phase 180 pushing every pixel the other way (010); repeat keeps the top row's covering and is otherwise 003 (011); the keyed height and the overshooting speed, held at 360, meet the plain cases at their frames (012, 013); moved, the wave moves with the drawing, the grown columns show the pushed stripes with transparent and stay empty with repeat (014, 015); and height 2.5 grows by 3 (016).

FX-WAVE-001: The settings as they start: shape sine, height 10, width 40, direction 90, speed 0, phase 0, edges transparent. The wave runs to the right and pushes each column down by 10 sin(2 pi X / 40), more than the drawing's height across its middle: column 0 is pushed down by 0.8 pixels, column 3 by 5.2, columns 7 to 12 by more than 9, so their rows 0 to 8 are empty and row 9 keeps only part of the drawing's top row, and column 15 by 6.5; the frames are the same, the wave standing still at speed 0.

FX-WAVE-003: Height 2, width 8: a wave every eight pixels, each column pushed down or up by 2 sin(2 pi X / 8), so the blue band waves: columns 1 and 2 carry it down into rows 6 and 7 and columns 5 and 6 up into rows 2 and 3. ## Ripple fixtures

D-150, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/ripple/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Ripple (`core.ripple`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/ripple/media/stripes.png`, Turbulent Displace's: in rows 1 to 8 and columns 0 to 13, upright stripes two pixels wide, skin #f6d6be and line #1e1a24 by turns (columns 0 and 1 skin, 2 and 3 line, and so on), crossed by a blue band #3a6fd8 in rows 4 and 5; column 14 is the skin at half covering, a soft edge; column 15 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. The centre as it starts, 50, 50, is the point (8, 5), in the middle of the band. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/ripple_reference.py`**, which works D-150's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/ripple/expected_ripple.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. The rule has no cliff: the bilinear sample moves smoothly with the point it reads, and the one choice it makes, a pixel at no distance from the centre, is met only where the reach is 0 either way (FX-RIPPLE-009, 010).

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers, and that every pixel's colour stays within its covering (all): as it starts, every pixel reads from further out on frame 0, so more than 60 more pixels are empty, and on frames 2 and 4 every pixel inside the still ring, 3.33 and 6.67 pixels out, reads from nearer the centre and every pixel outside it from further out (001); amplitude 0 changes nothing (002); with speed 0 the rings hold still (003); speed 90 comes back to FX-RIPPLE-003 after a full turn and is phase 180 half way, which reads every pixel the same distance the other way (004, 005); a longer wavelength differs (006); speed -90 differs from speed 90 at a quarter turn and meets it at half a turn (007); with fade 6 every pixel six or more from the centre is its own and every nearer one reaches less far (008); a pixel at the centre is its own, and with a fade of half a pixel nothing changes (009, 010); the centre in the corner, and keyed, meets the plain cases at its frames (011, 012); the keyed amplitude, and the overshooting fade held at 0, meet the plain cases at their frames (013, 014); moved, the ripple moves with the drawing and nothing grows (015); wavelength 1 breaks the stripes up (016); speed 360 stands still to within rounding (017); and phase 40 is two frames of speed 20 (018).

FX-RIPPLE-001: The settings as they start: centre 50, 50, the point (8, 5), amplitude 5, wavelength 30, speed 20, phase 0, fade 0. Each pixel reads from up to five pixels along its line through the centre. On frame 0 every pixel reads from further out, so the drawing is drawn in toward the centre, a small patch with empty all round it. The rings move outward: the still ring, where nothing moves, is at the centre on frame 0, 3.33 pixels out on frame 2 and 6.67 on frame 4, and inside it each pixel reads from nearer the centre, so the middle of the band is magnified while the rest is still drawn in; the three frames differ.

## Twirl fixtures

D-151, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/twirl/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Twirl (`core.twirl`) on it, unmoved unless the case says; FX-TWIRL-015 puts a directional blur ahead of it. The drawing is `Fixtures/twirl/media/cross.png`: a card filling the frame, skin #f6d6be crossed by the line #1e1a24 down column 8 and along row 5, the skin's shadow #dca08c in rows 8 and 9, column 0 the skin at half covering, a soft edge, and the top right corner, columns 14 and 15 of rows 0 and 1, empty. The middle of the drawing, the centre as it starts, is the point (8, 5), the corner where four pixels meet at the crossing, so the twirl bends both lines into a spiral the owner can see. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/twirl_reference.py`**, which works D-151's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/twirl/expected_twirl.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers, and the rule's pieces: a positive angle turns the picture clockwise (a pixel right of the centre takes its picture from above it), the turn is the angle at the centre and falls off with the square of the distance to none at the radius, each pixel samples at its own distance from the centre, and no fixture pixel sits within 1e-5 of a radius, so none is on the edge between kept and turned; every case keeps each channel inside its covering. As it starts every pixel is turned, by about 87 degrees beside the centre and 61 at the corners, the lines leave their column and row, and column 15 and the lower part of column 0 are emptied (001); a negative angle samples the mirror image of those points across the line from the centre (002); angle 0 or radius 0 change nothing (003, 004); a small radius, or a centre in the corner, turns only the pixels inside the circle and keeps every other exactly (005, 006, 009); the most angle differs from the start (007); radius 10000 is within a fifth of a degree of a quarter turn, the lines swapped over and the drawing standing on end in columns 3 to 12 (008); the keyed settings meet the plain cases at their frames, an overshooting ease held at 3600 (010 to 013); moved, the twirl moves with the drawing and nothing is drawn left of it (014); and after a directional blur the centre is the drawing's own, not a point of the grown layer (015).

FX-TWIRL-001: The settings as they start: angle 90, radius 50, about the middle, the point (8, 5). The whole drawing lies inside the circle, so every pixel is turned clockwise, by about 87 degrees beside the centre and by about 61 at the corners: the two lines bend into a spiral about the middle, and column 15 and rows 2 to 9 of column 0, which take their picture from past the drawing's top and bottom edges, are empty. Pixels deep in the skin take skin and look unchanged.

## Bulge fixtures

D-152, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/bulge/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Bulge (`core.bulge`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/bulge/media/stripes.png`: in rows 1 to 8 and columns 0 to 13, upright stripes two pixels wide, skin #f6d6be and line #1e1a24 by turns (line in columns 2, 3, 6, 7, 10 and 11), crossed by a blue band #3a6fd8 in rows 4 and 5; column 14 is the skin at half covering, a soft edge; column 15 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. The drawing's middle, (8, 5), falls on the corner between four band pixels. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/bulge_reference.py`**, which works D-152's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, with document 21's bilinear sample imported from `tools/radial_blur_reference.py`. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/bulge/expected_bulge.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. The rule has no cliff: at the circle's edge the pull is 0, so the warp meets the kept pixels without a seam.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every channel stays within its covering (all); as it starts every pixel is pulled between a third and a half of the way in, the band spreads into rows 3 and 6 and the empty edges fill (001); height 0 and radius 0 change nothing (002, 003); with radius 6 every pixel 6 or more from the centre is kept exactly and those inside change, for a swell, a pinch whose every sample lies farther out, and the hardest pinch (004, 005, 007); at height 4 the twelve pixels within 1.76 of the middle all read the middle point, the band's blue (006); the moved centre keeps every column from 10 on (008); a centre on a pixel's own centre keeps that pixel (009); a circle wholly off the drawing changes nothing (010); the keyed height, radius and centre, and the overshooting ease held at 4, meet the plain cases at their frames (011 to 014); moved, the swell moves with the drawing and nothing grows (015); near the soft edge the empty column 15 takes part of the covering inside the circle and stays empty past it (016); and at radius 10000 every pixel is pulled within a hundredth of a pixel of half way (017).

FX-BULGE-001: The settings as they start: centre 50, 50, radius 50, height 1. The circle is far larger than the drawing, so every pixel is pulled toward the middle, by about half at the middle and a third at the corners: the whole drawing is magnified about the middle, the blue band spreading into rows 3 and 6, and the empty top and bottom rows and right-hand column filled from inside.

## Mirror fixtures

D-153, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/mirror/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Mirror (`core.mirror`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/mirror/media/arrow.png`: an arrow pointing right, a blue shaft #3a6fd8 in rows 4 and 5, columns 2 to 10, a red head #c82828 in columns 11 to 13 (rows 2 to 7, 3 to 6, 4 and 5), tipped by the skin #f6d6be at half covering in column 14, rows 4 and 5, a soft tip; above it on the left a dark block, the line #1e1a24, in rows 1 and 2, columns 1 to 3, with a half-covering edge in column 4; below it a skin block in rows 7 and 8, columns 5 to 9, across the middle; everything else empty. Its left and right halves and its top and bottom halves all differ, so every reflection shows. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/mirror_reference.py`**, which works D-153's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/mirror/expected_mirror.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: at angles 0, 90, 180 and 270 about the middle, the kept half is the drawing's exactly and each pixel of the other half is the drawing's pixel mirrored across the line, right, bottom, left and top kept in turn (001 to 004), a whole turn and a quarter turn back giving the same pictures (005, 006); at 45 each pixel above and left of the corner-wise line takes the pixel with row and column swapped about it (007), and at 30 the kept side is exact while the reflected side has blends of neighbours (008); a centre on a pixel's middle keeps that column and mirrors about it (009), and a centre a quarter into a pixel gives each reflected pixel an even blend of two (010); moving the centre moves the line (011), the left edge keeps everything (012), the right edge leaves every pixel empty (013), and at angle 0 the centre's height changes nothing (014); the keyed centre and angle meet the plain cases at their frames, an overshooting ease held at 3600 where 4770 would have turned it a quarter more (015 to 017); and moved, the effect moves with the drawing and nothing grows (018). The rule's pieces are checked too: the direction is exact at quarter turns, and on the line the reflection is the point itself, so the two sides meet without a seam and the choice is not a cliff.

## Motion Tile fixtures

D-154, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/motion_tile/`, holding one drawing 6 by 4 with one Motion Tile (`core.motion_tile`) on it, its centre on the composition's centre, so its top left corner is at (5, 3), unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/motion_tile/media/patch.png`, turned neither way alike so a tile turned over shows: skin #f6d6be in columns 0 to 3 of rows 0 to 2, a red dot #c82828 at (1, 1), the skin at half covering at (0, 2), a soft edge, a line #1e1a24 down column 4 in rows 0 to 2, and a blue band #3a6fd8 along row 3 from column 2 and up column 5 into row 2; (5, 0), (5, 1), (0, 3) and (1, 3) are empty. Positions below are the composition's. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, or empty, exactly. A layer that grows is shown with its grown pixels in place, so the tiles land around the drawing.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/motion_tile_reference.py`**, which works D-154's rule from the drawing's 8-bit values: each output pixel is one input pixel, copied exactly, so there is no mixing. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/motion_tile/expected_motion_tile.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers, and works every tiled frame a second way, a mirrored run as the tile and its reflection repeating every two widths: every pixel is one of the drawing's or empty (all); the growth is 6 (p / 100 - 1) / 2 across and 4 (p / 100 - 1) / 2 down rounded up, and no growth it decides is within 1e-5 of a whole number unless it is one worked exactly (all); the start settings and mirror on at 100 change nothing (001, 002); width 200 repeats columns 3 to 5 on the left and 0 to 2 on the right, the red dot at (12, 4) (003); height 200 repeats rows 2 and 3 above and 0 and 1 below (004); both 200 fill columns 2 to 13 and rows 1 to 8 with 80 covered pixels (005); mirror on meets each edge with its own reflection, the red dot at (3, 4), (6, 1) and (3, 1) (006); 300 tiles the whole frame, and with mirror on repeats every 12 columns and 8 rows (007, 008); 1000 is 300 in the frame (009); 150 grows by 2 and 1, to 10 by 6 (010); 110 and 125 add one pixel on every side, from the opposite edge, or with mirror on the edge's own, the soft edge held outward (011, 012); the keyed width meets width 200 at frame 2 and 300 at frame 4, and the overshooting height, held at 1000, is the same at frames 2 and 4 (013, 014); moved, the tiles move with the layer (015); and after a drop shadow the tiles are the grown 10 by 8 layer's, shadow and all (016).

## Linear Wipe fixtures

D-155, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/linear_wipe/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Linear Wipe (`core.linear_wipe`) on it, unmoved unless the case says; FX-LWIPE-021 to 024 put a drop shadow ahead of it (black, opacity 100, direction 270, distance 2, softness 0), which grows the layer two pixels on every side, and move the layer three pixels right so the shadow's grown columns show. The drawing is `Fixtures/linear_wipe/media/cel.png`, a cel filling the frame: rows 0 and 9 empty; the line #1e1a24 at half covering down column 0 and the skin #f6d6be at half covering down column 15, soft edges; a box of line round columns 1 to 14 and rows 1 to 8; inside it the skin in rows 2 and 3, white left of a red #c82828 patch in rows 4 and 5 with an empty hole in columns 7 and 8, and the shadow skin #dca08c in rows 6 and 7. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/linear_wipe_reference.py`**, which works D-155's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/linear_wipe/expected_linear_wipe.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every pixel is its input times one part from 0 to 1, the same on all four channels, the empty pixels stay empty, and with feather 0 every pixel is its input exactly or gone, none within 1e-5 of the edge, the cliff (all); completion 0 changes nothing and 100 leaves nothing (001, 004, 014); the edge's place for completion 25, 50 and 75 from the left (002, 003, 015), from the right, the bottom and the top (006, 007, 008) and on a diagonal (009); the feathered edge's parts, 1/8 to 7/8 over four pixels and about half everywhere at 10000 (005, 013), and a soft diagonal growing towards the bottom right (010); angles a whole turn apart are the same (011, 012); the keyed, held and overshooting settings meet the plain cases at their frames (015 to 019); moved, the edge moves with the drawing (020); and after a drop shadow, completion 0 keeps the shadow's grown columns, the edge passes over them as over the drawing, and completion 100 clears them too (021 to 024).

## Radial Wipe fixtures

D-156, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/radial_wipe/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Radial Wipe (`core.radial_wipe`) on it, unmoved unless the case says; FX-RWIPE-021 puts a directional blur ahead of it. The drawing is `Fixtures/radial_wipe/media/cross.png`: a card filling the frame, skin #f6d6be crossed by the line #1e1a24 down column 8 and along row 5, the skin's shadow #dca08c in rows 8 and 9, column 0 the skin at half covering, a soft edge, and the top right corner, columns 14 and 15 of rows 0 and 1, empty. The middle of the drawing, the centre as it starts, is the point (8, 5), the corner where four pixels meet at the crossing, so a quarter turn swept from straight up takes exactly the top right quarter, and the owner can see each sweep as whole quarters and halves of the card. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/radial_wipe_reference.py`**, which works D-156's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/radial_wipe/expected_radial_wipe.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers, and the rule's pieces: the screen angle is 0 straight up and 90 to the right, counterclockwise measures the other way round, both is the same either side of the start line, a negative start angle is that angle plus 360, and completion 0 changes nothing even with a feather; every case keeps each pixel a part of itself, the same part for all four channels, so a soft edge stays soft and an empty pixel empty; and no fixture pixel, grown ones too, sits within 1e-5 of the hard edge or of the start line, the two places a pixel is decided all or nothing. As it starts nothing changes (001); completion 25, 50 and 75 take the top right quarter, the right half and all but the top left quarter, keeping the rest exactly, and 100 leaves every pixel transparent (002 to 005); counterclockwise takes the top left quarter, both the top half, and a start angle of 90 the bottom right quarter (006 to 008); a start angle of 30 slants the edge (009); a feather of 90 fades the sweeping edge over 90 degrees while the start line stays hard, and a feather of 360 keeps each pixel its angle over 360 of itself (010, 011); counterclockwise from straight down with a feather softens only the far edge (012); a centre in the corner sweeps from there (013); the keyed settings meet the plain cases at their frames, a held key jumps and an overshooting ease is held at 100 (014 to 019); moved, the wipe moves with the drawing (020); and after a directional blur the grown pixels are wiped by the same rule about the drawing's own centre (021).

## Venetian Blinds fixtures

D-157, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/venetian_blinds/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Venetian Blinds (`core.venetian_blinds`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/venetian_blinds/media/window.png`: a window, columns 0 and 15 empty, columns 1 and 14 the line #1e1a24 at half covering, a soft frame down both sides, and between them, columns 2 to 13, sky #3a6fd8 in rows 0 to 4 and skin #f6d6be in rows 5 to 9, with a red sill #c82828 across row 7, columns 4 to 11. Every row and every column holds shown pixels, so every slat shows, and the empty and soft pixels show that only the covering changes. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/venetian_blinds_reference.py`**, which works D-157's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/venetian_blinds/expected_venetian_blinds.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: the starting settings change nothing (001); at width 4 and completion 50 the level slats lose rows 2, 3, 6 and 7, the upright ones at 90 columns 0, 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12 and 13, at 180 and 270 the other halves (002, 005 to 007), exactly, every other pixel the drawing's; the starting width 20 is taller than the drawing, so completion 60 clears only rows 8 and 9 (003); completion 100 empties every pixel, feathered too (004); at angle 30 every pixel is kept exactly or cleared, about half each (008), angle -270 is angle 90 exactly (009), and width 2 clears every other row (010); feather 2 puts each slat's moving edge at half covering, feather 4 grades each slat's rows 1, 1, 0.95, 0.7 and 0.45 with a hard jump back at the next slat, and the most feather fades everything to within 0.0002 of half (011 to 013); the keyed completion and angle meet the plain cases at their frames, a cleared pixel never comes back, and an overshooting ease is held at 100 (014 to 017); and moved, the slats move with the drawing (018). Every case scales each pixel's four channels by one number 0 to 1 and leaves the empty pixels empty. The rule's pieces are checked too: the direction is exact at quarter turns, and without a feather no decided pixel sits within 1e-5 of the moving edge or, in any case, of a slat's own edge, the two cliffs.

## Iris Wipe fixtures

D-158, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/iris_wipe/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Iris Wipe (`core.iris_wipe`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/iris_wipe/media/cel.png`: in rows 1 to 8 and columns 0 to 13, a box of line #1e1a24 (column 0 and rows 1 and 8) filled with skin #f6d6be and crossed by a blue band #3a6fd8 in rows 4 and 5; column 14 is the skin at half covering, a soft edge; column 15 and rows 0 and 9 are empty. The drawing's middle, (8, 5), falls on the corner between four band pixels, and its farthest corner is the square root of 89, 9.434, from there. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/iris_wipe_reference.py`**, which works D-158's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/iris_wipe/expected_iris_wipe.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. With no feather the wipe is a cliff, a pixel kept or gone by its distance from the centre; the tool asserts that no pixel it decides lies within 1e-5 of the circle.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every pixel is the drawing's times one amount from 0 to 1 on all four channels, an empty pixel stays empty, and with no feather no pixel sits within 1e-5 of the circle (all); as it starts nothing changes, and completion 100 leaves every pixel transparent (001, 002); at completion 50 exactly the 68 pixels inside the circle of radius 4.717 are kept, and inverted exactly those are gone, the two adding up to the drawing (003, 004); at 25 the 128 pixels inside are kept and the 32 outside, columns 0 and 15 and the rows' ends, are gone (005); at 75 only the four by four block about the middle is kept, and the inverted wipe at 25 is its exact opposite (006, 007); with feather 4 each pixel is faded by the rule's amount, whole within 2.717 of the middle and gone from 6.717, falling with the distance, the soft column faded further, and the inverted soft wipe is its opposite (008, 009); feather 10000 fades every pixel to within a thousandth of half (010); completion 0 and 100 win over every other setting (011, 012); the moved centres keep exactly the pixels inside their own circles (013, 014); the keyed completion, centre and feather, and the overshooting ease held at 100, meet the plain cases at their frames, the circle closing frame by frame (015 to 018); and moved, the wipe moves with the drawing and nothing grows (019).

## Simple Choker fixtures

D-159, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/simple_choker/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Simple Choker (`core.simple_choker`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/simple_choker/media/matte.png`: a box of line #1e1a24 in columns 4 to 10 and rows 2 to 7, filled with skin #f6d6be, with a one-pixel hole at (7, 4) and the skin at half covering (128) at (8, 6); the line at half covering at (11, 4), its antialiased edge; a one-pixel speck of line at (13, 8); and a blue block #3a6fd8 in columns 0 to 2 and rows 6 to 9, touching the drawing's left and bottom edges, one empty column from the box. The rest is empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly. A layer that grows is shown with its grown pixels in place, so in the moved spread case the columns left of the drawing are the grown pixels.

## Speed Lines fixtures

D-160, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/speed_lines/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Speed Lines (`core.speed_lines`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. Speed Lines is a generator, so the drawing is mostly `Fixtures/speed_lines/media/solid.png`, a white solid #ffffff covering the frame, where a pixel's red value is 1 less the line strength q laid on it; FX-SPEED-021 uses `Fixtures/speed_lines/media/card.png`, Noise's card: column 0 and row 9 empty, column 15 the skin #f6d6be at half covering, and in rows 0 to 8 a box of line #1e1a24 in columns 3 to 12 and rows 1 to 7, filled with skin, with a white patch in columns 5 and 6 and a black one in columns 9 and 10 of rows 3 and 4, on grey #808080. The centre as it starts, 50, 50, is the point (8, 5), between the four middle pixels. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/speed_lines_reference.py`**, which works D-160's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, every line counted, with Noise's hash from `tools/noise_reference.py`. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/speed_lines/expected_speed_lines.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. The rule has no cliff: every step of it is continuous, so no pixel needs keeping away from one.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every covering, leaves the empty pixels empty and every channel inside its covering (all); as it starts every line begins at least 90 pixels out, past the whole drawing, so nothing changes (001); with inner 0 every pixel is greyed and none black, frame 1 is frame 0 and frames 2 and 4 are new lines (002); twelve wide lines make some pixels black and leave some white, on twos (003); evenly spaced, columns 7 and 8 match on the upright lines and the pixels under 1.5 from the centre are untouched (004); inner jitter 100 reaches pixels under 4.5 that inner jitter 0 leaves and leaves some it reaches (005); angle jitter 100 moves the lines, each within 15 degrees of its even place (006); thickness 30 darkens no pixel less and the whole more than half as much again (007); thickness 0 leaves no pixel more than half way (008); count 4 makes a cross with the diagonals between its arms untouched (009); count 1000 at thickness 30 blacks every pixel 4 or more from the centre (010); seed 7.9 is seed 7 and not seed 0 (011); hold 1 meets 003's frames 2 and 4 at frames 1 and 2, and hold 100 keeps frame 0 (012, 013); opacity 50 halves every q (014); the blue lies each pixel q of the way to #3a6fd8, and capitals are the same (015, 016); centred on the left edge the edge's middle pixels are untouched (017); the keyed count meets the plain counts 4, 8, 12 and 20 at frames 0, 1, 2 and 4, and the overshooting opacity is held at 100 (018, 019); moved, the lines move with the drawing (020); and on the card each shown pixel is moved toward black by 003's q, the soft edge keeping its half covering, the black patch black and the empty pixels empty (021).

## Cross Glare fixtures

D-161, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/cross_glare/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Cross Glare (`core.cross_glare`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/cross_glare/media/sparks.png`: a warm yellow point (250, 220, 120), brightest channel 98 %, at column 2, row 4, near the left edge; a purple bar #3c286e, 43 %, down column 5, rows 1 to 8, which the streaks cross; the yellow at half covering, a soft point, at column 12, row 2; and a brown point (153, 102, 51), exactly 60 %, at column 12, row 7. Everything else is empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly. A layer that grows is shown with its grown pixels in place, so in the moved case the columns left of the drawing are the grown pixels.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/cross_glare_reference.py`**, which works D-161's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, with D-89's bright test (`tools/glow_reference.py`) and `tools/radial_blur_reference.py`'s bilinear rule. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/cross_glare/expected_cross_glare.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case takes nothing away and keeps its covering in 0..1 (all); the bright test is D-89's, the weights sum to one and the streak directions are exact at quarter turns and spread evenly; as it starts, both bright points are streaked along both diagonals, the soft point's streaks 128/255 of the yellow's, the brown and the purple give no light and pixels well off the diagonals are untouched (001); intensity 0, length 0.9 and threshold 100 change nothing (002 to 004); length 4 is stronger near the point, crosses the purple bar and ends four steps out (005); threshold 60 lights the brown (006); one point streaks up-right only, two points up-right and down-left (007, 008); angle 0 is a plus landing on whole pixels, with the weights 0.64/1.2 and 0.16/1.2 exactly, and angle 90 is the same (009, 010); angle 405 and points 4.9 are 005 exactly, and points 6 differs (011 to 013); intensity 2.5 is 2.5 times the streaks, past white (014); orange, its capitals and black change only the colour (015 to 017); the keyed length, the keyed points, floored to 4 at frame 2, and the overshooting intensity, held at 10, meet the plain cases at their frames (018 to 020); and moved, the plus moves with the drawing and its left streak shows on the two grown columns left of the drawing, the third staying empty (021).

FX-GLARE-001: The settings as they start: threshold 80, length 40, points 4, angle 45, intensity 1, white. The yellow, 98 %, and the soft yellow are bright enough; the brown, 60 %, and the purple give no light. Each bright point is streaked along both diagonals, an X, faint as the light is shared over forty steps, running on past the frame; the soft point's streaks are half as strong. The diagonals run between pixel centres, so each streak is spread a little onto the pixels beside its line, and the yellow even takes a little of its own light; pixels well off the diagonals stay as they were.

## Camera Shake fixtures

D-162, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/camera_shake/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Camera Shake (`core.camera_shake`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is Wave Warp's, `Fixtures/camera_shake/media/stripes.png`: in rows 0 to 8 and columns 0 to 13, upright stripes two pixels wide, skin #f6d6be and line #1e1a24 by turns starting with skin, crossed by a blue band #3a6fd8 in rows 4 and 5, touching the drawing's top and left edges; column 14 is the skin at half covering, a soft edge; column 15 and row 9 are empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly. A layer that grows is shown with its grown pixels in place, so in the moved cases the columns left of the drawing are the grown pixels.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/camera_shake_reference.py`**, which works D-162's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, the jolts from Noise's hash imported from `tools/noise_reference.py` and the sampling by `tools/radial_blur_reference.py`'s bilinear rule. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/camera_shake/expected_camera_shake.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers: every case keeps every pixel premultiplied with its covering in 0..1, and every case's pixels are the same when sampled past the grown layer, so the growth cuts nothing (all); as it starts, the five frames are five different moves, the ones the case names to two decimals, and frame 1 moves the drawing out of the frame, leaving it empty (001); amount 0 and rotation 0 change nothing (002); amount 2 gives five different frames, frame 0 carrying the band down into row 6 (003); hold 2 keeps each of 003's jolts for two frames and hold 5 keeps its first for all five (004, 005); hold 1.9 and seed 1.6 are floored, to 003 and to seed 1's 007, which differs from 003 (006 to 008); rotation 10 alone tilts the band up to the right at frame 0 and down to the right at frame 2 (009), and with amount 2 differs from both the move and the turn (010); the keyed amount and the overshooting rotation, held at 45, meet the plain cases at their frames (011, 012); and moved three pixels right, the jolt and the turn carry the drawing into the grown pixels, shown in the three columns left of it, every other column being the unmoved layer's three columns on (013, 014).

FX-SHAKE-001: The settings as they start: amount 10, rotation 0, hold 1, seed 0. Each frame the drawing jolts to a new place, up to 10 pixels each way, larger than the drawing itself: frame 0 moves it 0.57 pixels left and 2.96 down, frame 1 9.51 right and 9.94 up, out of the frame, so frame 1 is empty, frame 2 6.04 left and 1.57 up, frame 3 1.54 right and 0.47 down, and frame 4 8.05 left and 6.89 down.

## Rain fixtures

D-163, accepted on 2026-09-26. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/rain/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Rain (`core.rain`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. Rain is a generator, so most cases lay it on `Fixtures/rain/media/night.png`, a solid of the line's colour #1e1a24 covering the whole frame; FX-RAIN-019 lays it on `Fixtures/rain/media/card.png`, Noise's card (column 0 and row 9 empty, column 15 the skin at half covering, a box of line #1e1a24 in columns 3 to 12 and rows 1 to 7 filled with skin #f6d6be, a white patch in columns 5 and 6 and a black one in columns 9 and 10, both in rows 3 and 4, on a grey card #808080), to show the rain stays inside a drawing's covering. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/rain_reference.py`**, which works D-163's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, with Noise's hash from `tools/noise_reference.py`. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/rain/expected_rain.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks each case's claim on its numbers, reading each pixel's strength back from its colour: no cell any case reaches holds its drop within 1e-5 of the density (all, the closest 0.0015); every case keeps every pixel's covering, leaves the empty pixels empty and moves each pixel toward the rain's colour by no more than the opacity (all); as it starts the small frame sees no drop at frames 0 and 4 and one streak of 10 to 20 pixels at frame 3 (001); spacing 4 shows at least 20 rainy pixels (002); density 0 and opacity 0 change nothing (003, 006); density 100 keeps every drop of 002 and adds more (004); opacity 100 is 002's strength unscaled (005); width 3 is at least as rainy as 002, width 0 at most half strength and length 0 at most as rainy (007, 008, 009); straight down at one pixel a frame, frames 1 and 4 are frame 0 moved one and four pixels down, and direction 540 is the same (010, 011); the streaks run down the columns at direction 180 and along the rows at direction 90, where speed 0 keeps frame 4 as frame 0 (010, 012); seed 7 differs and 7.9 is 7 (013, 014); capitals change nothing (015); the keyed opacity and the overshooting density, held at 100, meet the plain cases at their frames (016, 017); moved, the rain moves with the drawing (018); and on the card every pixel that shows takes 002's strength, the soft edge at its half covering (019).

FX-RAIN-001: The settings as they start: colour #c8d8ff, density 30, spacing 24, length 20, width 1, direction 170, speed 30, seed 0, opacity 60, on the night solid. The frame is smaller than one cell of the field, so it sees few drops: none at frame 0, one long pale streak drifting a little right, at frame 3, and none again at frame 4, the rain having fallen 30 pixels a frame past it.

## Preset file fixtures

D-180, accepted on 2026-09-28. `tools/preset_file_reference.py` writes `Fixtures/preset_file/`: nineteen preset files and `expected_preset_file.json`. Its effects are taken from committed fixture projects, so each is one the build already reads. A valid case gives the presets the build must read, by name and effect type, in order; the build's test also writes each back and reads it again, and must get the same presets. A refused case gives the diagnostic and a word its message must contain, and the build must import nothing from it.

`check` confirms every valid file keeps the rule on its own terms (the two keys, version 0, names present and unrepeated, every preset with effects), that the two effect refusals differ from a valid file only by the unknown effect or setting, that the not-JSON file is not JSON and that the project file is a project.

| case | file | says | the build reads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FX-PRE-001 | `fx_pre_001.fxpreset` | One preset holding one effect: the smallest file. | "Soft glow": core.glow |
| FX-PRE-002 | `fx_pre_002.fxpreset` | Three presets, read in the file's order, each with its effects in their order. | "Night": core.invert, core.vignette; "Poster": core.posterize; "Lifted": core.drop_shadow, core.glow, core.posterize |
| FX-PRE-003 | `fx_pre_003.fxpreset` | A keyed setting: the keys come with the preset, at the frames they were at. | "Flash": core.exposure |
| FX-PRE-004 | `fx_pre_004.fxpreset` | An effect switched off stays off. | "Off for now": core.glow, core.invert |
| FX-PRE-005 | `fx_pre_005.fxpreset` | A name in Japanese, with inner spaces, is kept exactly as written. | "撃ち合い  光 2": core.glow |
| FX-PRE-006 | `fx_pre_006.fxpreset` | A setting outside its range is read and kept, as a project file's is (D-46); the effect is not drawn where the preset is applied, and the layer says why. | "Wrong radius": core.glow |
| FX-PRE-007 | `fx_pre_007.fxpreset` | The same effect id in two presets does not matter: pasting gives each new ids. | "A": core.glow; "B": core.glow |
| FX-PRE-008 | `fx_pre_008.fxpreset` | Names differing only by capitals are two presets. | "glow": core.glow; "Glow": core.glow |
| FX-PRE-009 | `fx_pre_009.fxpreset` | Not JSON: a text file chosen by mistake. | refused, `PRESET_FILE_INVALID`, naming JSON |
| FX-PRE-010 | `fx_pre_010.fxpreset` | A project file chosen by mistake is named as one. | refused, `PRESET_FILE_INVALID`, naming project |
| FX-PRE-011 | `fx_pre_011.fxpreset` | A newer version is refused, never guessed at. | refused, `PRESET_FILE_INVALID`, naming newer |
| FX-PRE-012 | `fx_pre_012.fxpreset` | Something the rule does not name, beside the presets, would be lost, so the file is refused. | refused, `PRESET_FILE_INVALID`, naming author |
| FX-PRE-013 | `fx_pre_013.fxpreset` | Something the rule does not name, in a preset, likewise. | refused, `PRESET_FILE_INVALID`, naming thumbnail |
| FX-PRE-014 | `fx_pre_014.fxpreset` | A name of spaces only. | refused, `PRESET_FILE_INVALID`, naming name |
| FX-PRE-015 | `fx_pre_015.fxpreset` | Two presets with one name: which one was meant is not known. | refused, `PRESET_FILE_INVALID`, naming Soft glow |
| FX-PRE-016 | `fx_pre_016.fxpreset` | A preset with no effects. | refused, `PRESET_FILE_INVALID`, naming Empty |
| FX-PRE-017 | `fx_pre_017.fxpreset` | A file with no presets. | refused, `PRESET_FILE_INVALID`, naming presets |
| FX-PRE-018 | `fx_pre_018.fxpreset` | An effect this build does not have, in the last of three presets, refuses the whole file: the first two are not taken either. | refused, `EFFECT_UNSUPPORTED`, naming core.lens_sparkle |
| FX-PRE-019 | `fx_pre_019.fxpreset` | A setting this build does not have would be lost, so the file is refused. | refused, `EFFECT_UNSUPPORTED`, naming sparkle |

## Starter preset fixtures

D-181, accepted on 2026-09-28. `tools/starter_presets_reference.py` writes `Fixtures/starter_presets/`: `starter.fxpreset`, the starter presets themselves, and `expected_starter_presets.json`, what the build must show: the presets in order, each one's effect types, the sentence the Effects panel shows, and where the build's pictures put it (`layer`: on `layer-3` of the reference shot; `adjustment`: on an adjustment layer above all four). Each effect is taken from a committed fixture project with only its settings changed.

`check` confirms the file keeps the preset file rule (the two keys, version 0, names present, unrepeated and trimmed), that there are six to ten, that every effect is switched on, every setting it names is inside its range and every word is one the effect has, and that no instance id repeats. The build's test must read the file with `persist::read_presets`, get these names and types, and draw each preset on frame 100 of the reference shot with no diagnostic and a picture different from the one without it.

| # | preset | pictured on | effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Soft bloom | adjustment | `core.bloom` |
| 2 | Night | adjustment | `core.color_balance`, `core.vibrance`, `core.brightness_contrast`, `core.vignette` |
| 3 | Sunset | adjustment | `core.color_balance`, `core.gradient` |
| 4 | Cel shadow | layer | `core.drop_shadow` |
| 5 | Rim light | layer | `core.rim_light` |
| 6 | Old film | adjustment | `core.gradient_map`, `core.noise`, `core.vignette`, `core.exposure_flicker` |
| 7 | Impact | adjustment | `core.cross_glare`, `core.chromatic_aberration`, `core.camera_shake` |
| 8 | Dream haze | adjustment | `core.diffusion`, `core.vibrance` |
| 9 | Speed lines | adjustment | `core.speed_lines` |

## Color Lookup fixtures

D-182, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/cube_lut/`, holding the Invert fixtures' drawing of colour bands (`media/bands.png`, described under Invert fixtures) with one Color Lookup (`core.color_lookup`) on it, and a lookup asset `asset-lut` whose file is under `luts/`, unmoved unless the case says. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change are listed: every other pixel is the drawing's own, exactly.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/cube_lut_reference.py`**, which reads each .cube file by document 19's rule and works D-182's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/cube_lut/expected_color_lookup.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks that every file reads back as written, in its dimensions, and every refused file is refused for its reason; that a 1D table is each channel through its own column and a 3D identity gives each colour back; that every case keeps every pixel's covering and leaves the empty pixels empty; the colours each case names (002 to 006); that no file chosen, a missing file and a setting naming no lookup asset leave the drawing exactly (007, 009 to 011); that moved, the look moves with the drawing (008); and that on an adjustment layer it is the same as on the drawing (012).
