FX-LUT-013: The lookup asset's file is luts/refused/count.cube, one line short: the drawing, untouched, with MEDIA_DECODE_FAILED at every frame and nothing on opening; the asset and the setting are kept. Checked by the build's test on its own, as the file-level check above compares what opening warns of with what a frame warns of. Frames 0 and 4: every pixel is the drawing's, unchanged.

**Refused files.** Each file under `Fixtures/cube_lut/luts/refused/` must be refused, whole, with this reason, word for word:

| file | reason |
| --- | --- |
| `refused/count.cube` | the table has 7 lines where LUT_3D_SIZE 2 needs 8 |
| `refused/both.cube` | the file gives both LUT_1D_SIZE and LUT_3D_SIZE, a 1D table before a 3D one, which this program does not read |
| `refused/no_size.cube` | the file gives no LUT_3D_SIZE or LUT_1D_SIZE |
| `refused/empty.cube` | the file gives no LUT_3D_SIZE or LUT_1D_SIZE |
| `refused/word.cube` | line 4: a table line must be three numbers |
| `refused/four.cube` | line 2: a table line must be three numbers |
| `refused/nan.cube` | line 2: a table line must be three numbers |
| `refused/late.cube` | line 3: DOMAIN_MIN comes after the table has begun |
| `refused/unknown.cube` | line 2: LUT_4D_SIZE is not a keyword of a .cube file this program reads |
| `refused/twice.cube` | line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE is given twice |
| `refused/big.cube` | line 1: LUT_3D_SIZE must be one whole number from 2 to 256 |
| `refused/half.cube` | line 1: LUT_3D_SIZE must be one whole number from 2 to 256 |
| `refused/domain_order.cube` | the domain's top must be above its bottom in each colour |
| `refused/domain_short.cube` | line 2: DOMAIN_MAX must be three numbers |
| `refused/domain_twice.cube` | the file gives its domain more than one way |
| `refused/range_short.cube` | line 2: LUT_1D_INPUT_RANGE must be two numbers |
| `refused/not_text.cube` | the file is not text |

**Collect Files.** Collect Files on FX-LUT-002 copies the lookup file beside the drawing, under its asset's folder, lists it in the manifest as a lookup file used by the layer whose effect names it, and the collected project names the copy; on FX-LUT-009 the missing file is listed as missing and the asset is kept. In the manifest, `media/asset-bands/bands.png` copied, `media/asset-lut/warm_17.cube` copied, `media/asset-lut/gone.cube` missing; the lookup asset's kind `lut`, used by `art` of `comp-main`.

## Line Blur fixtures

D-183, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/line_blur/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.line_blur` on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawings are in `Fixtures/line_blur/media/`: `bar.png`, a one-pixel line of `#1e1a24` across row 4, columns 4 to 11; `stairs.png`, a one-pixel diagonal of the same line drawn with no smoothing, in row `2 + x / 3` (whole division) at each column x; and `face.png`, line recolour's face, described under Line width fixtures. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that change by more than 1e-9 are listed: every other pixel is within 1e-9 of the drawing's own, far inside the tolerance.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/line_blur_reference.py`**, which works D-183's rule in double precision at every pixel of the composition from the drawings' 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/line_blur/expected_line_blur.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks that a clean straight line stays as it was at length 3 and at 50 (001, 010); that the crook of each step takes ink, the step beside it gives some up, and pixels more than one from the line stay nearly empty (002); that the face's straight sides, flat skin and the red line's middle stay, its ends change and the inside corners round off (003); that strength 50 is exactly halfway (004); that lines only is 003's change times each pixel's own ink (005); that length 0 and strength 0 leave the drawing exactly (006, 009); that keyed, the frames follow the length (007); that moved, the result moves with the drawing (008); and that no sample's covering came within 1e-5 of the stopping point 1/256, so single precision stops where double precision does.

FX-LBLUR-001: The bar, length 3: a clean straight line has nothing to smooth, and every pixel stays as it was, to within rounding.

Frame 0: every pixel is the drawing's, to within 1e-9.

FX-LBLUR-002: The stepped diagonal, length 4: the steps soften into a slope. The empty pixel in the crook of each step takes some ink, the step pixels give some up, and nothing more than one pixel from the line changes much.

## HSV key fixtures

D-184, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/hsv_key/`, holding one drawing the same size with `core.hsv_key` on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing, `Fixtures/hsv_key/media/screen.png`, is colour key's figure in front of a green screen, described under Colour key fixtures: the screen `#00b140` (hue 141.7, saturation 100, value 69.4), its shadow `#006424` in rows 8 and 9 (hue 141.6, value 39.2), the screen at half covering down column 15, an empty column 0, and a figure of line `#1e1a24` (hue 264) filled with skin `#f6d6be` (hue 25.7), with a grey button `#808080` at (7, 4) and spill `#5aa064` (hue 128.6, saturation 43.8) down column 4.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/hsv_key_reference.py`**, which works D-184's rule in double precision. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/hsv_key/expected_hsv_key.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. Every pixel of every frame either is the drawing's own value exactly or is 0 in all four channels, so each frame is written as the columns of each row that become 0; every other pixel is the drawing's.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks the colour conversion against values worked by hand, and each case's claim on its numbers. It also checks that no colour in any case lies within 1e-6 of a window's edge, except exactly on it where the arithmetic is exact in any precision (a grey's hue and saturation, 0; a colour with a channel at 0, saturation exactly 100), so the build cannot tip a pixel across an edge.

## Paraffin fixtures

D-185, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/paraffin/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Paraffin (`core.paraffin`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/paraffin/media/block.png`, Distance Gradation's block: rows 1 to 8, skin #f6d6be in columns 0 to 6 and shadow #dca08c in columns 7 to 9, a hole at (4, 4), the skin at half covering (128) down column 10, which is part of the figure, and at a quarter (64) down column 11, which is not but is washed as its place says, and a red dot #c82828 alone at (14, 4). Each value is a pixel's four working numbers, linear and premultiplied, red, green, blue and covering.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/paraffin_reference.py`**, which works D-185's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/paraffin/expected_paraffin.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks the blends and the curve against values worked by hand; the figure's extent from below (rows 1 to 8) and from the right (columns 0 to 14); that every case keeps every covering, leaves the empty pixels empty and passes no covering (all); that the wash grows row by row toward row 8 and leaves rows 1 and 2 untouched (001); that row 8 is wholly the violet and row 1 moved 1 - s s (3 - 2 s) of the way at s = 7/8 (002); the mirror from above (003); the dot wholly violet from the right and the wash growing column by column (004); rows 1 to 4 and the dot untouched at spread 50 (005); the corner order at 45 degrees (006); overlay moving further than soft light, and soft light lowering red and lifting blue (007, 008); multiply only darkening and screen only lightening (009, 010); add held at 1 (011); the untouched cases (012, 013); capitals (014); the keyed frames equal to the cases they name (015, 016); and the move (017).

FX-PARA-001: The settings as they start: #6450a0 from below (direction 180), spread 70, opacity 50, multiply. The block's bottom row, row 8, is darkened toward violet the most, each row above less, and rows 1 and 2, more than 70 per cent of the figure's eight rows up, not at all; the dot at (14, 4) is darkened as row 4 is; the empty pixels stay empty.

## Kira-kira fixtures

D-186, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/kira_kira/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Kira-kira (`core.kira_kira`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/kira_kira/media/glints.png`: a purple patch #3c286e in columns 1 to 6 and rows 1 to 7, with a cool white glint #fafaff at (2, 4) in it; the white two pixels square from (10, 2) to (11, 3) on the clear; the white at half covering (128) at (4, 8); a grey #999999, exactly 60 %, at (13, 8); and a gold #fadc78, bright but coloured, at (8, 7). Each value is a pixel's four working numbers, linear and premultiplied, red, green, blue and covering. The layer grows, and each frame shows its grown pixels in place: a pixel left of column 0 is not in the composition.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/kira_kira_reference.py`**, which works D-186's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/kira_kira/expected_kira_kira.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks that no cell any case reaches sits within 1e-5 of its density's cliff; the highlights, the gold one only at a threshold of 47 or under where D-89's test takes it at 95; the cells and which are chosen at seed 0; that no case takes light away or passes a covering of 1 (all); one star at the glints' middle, larger at frame 4 (001); the untouched cases (002 to 005); the three steady stars, the white point's arms on whole pixels exactly, the square's star on a pixel corner lighting both sides alike, and the grey, the gold and the pixels off the arms untouched (006); the diagonal arms (007); the X (008); the quarter turn (009); the grey's own star (010); one star at spacing 16 (011); the square's star gone and the others as before (012); other sizes at seed 7 (013); twinkling, and a whole period on as frame 0 (014); never below half (015); orange and capitals (016, 017); half strength (018); the keyed frames equal to the cases they name (019, 020); and the move, with the grown column lit (021).

FX-KIRA-001: The settings as they start: threshold 95, spacing 64, density 60, size 40, a star, angle 0, twinkle 100, period 24, seed 0, opacity 100, white. The frame is one cell, and it is chosen, so its three white glints, the point, the square and the soft one, share one star at their middle, (8.5, 4.17), on the clear; the grey, 60 %, is no highlight, nor is the gold, bright but coloured. At frame 0 the star is early in its twinkle and small; four frames later it is larger and brighter.

## Motion blur fixtures

**D-188, accepted by the owner on 2026-09-28 with ADR-019; built on the processor by B-124b the same day, checked by `verification/B-124b_motion_blur_table.md`.** The projects are in `Fixtures/motion_blur/`. The pixel cases are a composition 20 by 1 at 24 fps, three frames long, holding a bar 4 pixels wide and 1 high of the linear colour (1, 0.5, 0.25), anchor (0, 0), moving right 16 pixels a frame: its left edge at -10 on frame 0, 6 on frame 1 and 22 on frame 2. With a shutter of 180, a phase of -90 and 4 samples, frame 1 is drawn at 3, 5, 7 and 9, whole pixels, so every pixel is a count of quarters. Those are the composition's settings, and both switches are on, unless a case says otherwise. Each value is a pixel's four working numbers, red, green, blue and covering, linear and premultiplied. The times cases are the moments a frame is drawn at; the values cases are a property read between frames; FX-MB-050 is where a square's corners land on the screen at each moment, in 1920 by 1080, under a turning parent, an eased key, a curved path and a camera dolly. FX-MB-030 to 041 are files that must be refused.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/motion_blur_reference.py`**, which reads the very project files it writes and draws each frame pixel by pixel from documents 20 and 21, moving the bar by resampling where the build folds the transform and the camera into one matrix. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/motion_blur/expected_motion_blur.json`. Tolerance 1e-12 for the times and values, 1e-9 for the points, 1e-6 for the pixels.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks the still bar sharp (010); the staircase of 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1, 1 quarters (011); sharp with either switch off, with neither field, and at angle 0 (012, 013, 014, 017); the staircase moved on by 4 at phase 0 (015); sixteen quarters at 360 (016); the same staircase from a camera pan, a moving parent, a shape layer and a composition layer (018, 019, 027, 028); the held jump seen twice at half (020); opacity read at the frame (021); the in point (022); no red from the earlier drawing (023); the matte's cut (024, 025); the covering of 4 kept at 16 samples (026); and the moments and values of 001 to 008.

Times. Each row is the moments one frame is drawn at, first to last.

## Layer map fixtures

**D-189, accepted on 2026-09-28 by the owner's "take everything"; written by B-125a the same day, to be built by B-125b.** The project is `Fixtures/layer_map/layer_map.json`: the composition `comp-main`, 8 by 6 pixels and three frames at 24 fps, holding every layer the cases name, and `comp-inner`, 8 by 4 and two frames, holding one solid, `dot`. The drawings are in `Fixtures/layer_map/media/`: `card` 5 by 3, `card_b` its second cel, `big` 10 by 8 and `stripes` 8 by 8. Each case names the layer the effect is on (the holder), the layer its setting names, the fit, the frame, and Full or Draft, and gives the map the effect would read: its width and height and each pixel's four working numbers, red, green, blue and covering, linear and premultiplied; or no map; and what is said. No effect holds a layer setting until Compound Blur (A2), so B-125b checks these by making each map through the program directly. A2 adds the cases where an effect holds one: the setting kept when its layer is deleted, Undo bringing it back, the effect skipped, and a circle refused.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/effect_layer_reference.py`**, which reads the drawings it writes and works each map pixel by pixel from documents 20 and 21: the masks by ADR-016's sixteen samples, Exposure, the Gaussian blur, the Draft reads and the fits. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/layer_map/expected_layer_map.json`. Tolerance 1e-6.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks the card centred at (1, 1) with fifteen whole pixels (001); the same map moved, scaled, turned, faded and blended, switched off and matte-only, with its Exposure off, and at Draft on a solid (002, 003, 006, 032); the mask's cut (004); twice as bright (005); the blur cut back to the card (007); the layer's own drawing without its effect (008); the cel exposed, by the layer's own in point and offset (009 to 012); the solid, shape and composition layers' coverings (013 to 016); the empty maps and the two that say why (017 to 021); white through the adjustment layer's mask (020); a big picture tiling to its own centre (024); the card exact when stretched to its own size (027); the small holder centred and tiled (028, 029); stretch covering the holder and never tinting (025, 030); the Draft sizes (031, 033, 034); and no map for the three names that are no layer, only two of them said (040 to 042).

## Lightning Bolt fixtures

D-190, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/lightning_bolt/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Lightning Bolt (`core.lightning_bolt`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/lightning_bolt/media/night.png`: a night sky #1e2850 over columns 0 to 7, the right half, columns 8 to 15, empty. Each value is a pixel's four working numbers, linear and premultiplied, red, green, blue and covering.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/lightning_bolt_reference.py`**, which works D-190's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/lightning_bolt/expected_lightning_bolt.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks that no segment any case reaches has its fork choice within 1e-5 of the branches' cliff, nor a fork's side within 1e-5 of 0; that no case takes light away or passes a covering of 1 (all); that the bolt's ends stay on its points, a finer detail keeps every coarser point, and forks leave the main bolt where it was and thin to 0 at their tips; that the glow reaches every pixel and the bolt is held for two frames (001); the untouched cases (002, 003); the straight line, row 4 exactly the sky plus white and white on the clear (004); half and whole covering (005, 006); the glow's fall-off, 1, 4/9 and 1/9 (007), and the core over it (008); held and new bolts (009, 013); forks only adding (010); one bend (011); another seed (012); orange and green, and capitals (014, 015); half strength (016); the keyed frames equal to the cases they name (017, 018); the move, cut at the layer's edge (019); the round dot (020); and more light at the finest detail (021).

On a frame this small the glow reaches every pixel. Frames 0 and 1 are one bolt, held for two frames; frame 2 is a new one.

## Lightning Bolt Advanced Lightning fixtures

D-324, from D-308, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-04 (B-203). Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/lightning_extras/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Lightning Bolt (`core.lightning_bolt`) on it, its five new settings `kind`, `turbulence`, `decay`, `conductivity` and `obstacle` all written. The drawings are in `Fixtures/lightning_extras/media/`: `night.png`, D-190's (a night sky #1e2850 over columns 0 to 7, the right half empty); `ground.png`, rows 7 to 9 earth #5a3c1e, rows 0 to 6 empty; and `mist.png`, the same earth at half covering (128).

**Every number below is produced by `tools/lightning_extras_reference.py`**, which works document 21's D-324 rule on top of D-190's reference in double precision. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/lightning_extras/expected_lightning_extras.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. The types are this program's reading of Adobe's one-line descriptions; no After Effects frame was compared.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks that with all five at their starting values every FX-BOLT case's bolt is the same segment for segment and every unmoved one the same pixel for pixel; that no reached segment sits within 1e-5 of a fork's cliff, nor a fork's side within 1e-5 of 0; that an obstacle stops a bolt and its forks at the ground and leaves row 9 untouched (004, 006, 008) and the bolt runs on without one (005) or under the threshold (007); that Strike and Breaking keep FX-BOLT-010's main bolt; that Bouncy is three bolts, Omni six spokes of the end point's distance, the first towards it, Anywhere a new place each frame; that Vertical ignores the end point; that Two-Way's bolts meet in the middle; that turbulence adds forks; that decay thins the line along its length; and that conductivity starts at D-190's bolt and moves it smoothly.

FX-LIGHTX-001 (`fx_lightx_001.json`): FX-BOLT-001's settings with the five new ones written at their starting values (type direction, turbulence 0, decay 0, conductivity 0, obstacle 0): exactly FX-BOLT-001.

## Lightning Bolt round shapes fixtures

D-329, from P-26's tutorial 2 (B-211). Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/lightning_around/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Lightning Bolt (`core.lightning_bolt`) on it, D-324's five settings and the new word `path` all written. The drawings are in `Fixtures/lightning_around/media/`: `night.png`, `ground.png` and `mist.png`, D-324's; `block.png`, earth #5a3c1e across columns 5 to 10, rows 3 to 6, the rest empty; and `u.png`, an earth U, arms down columns 2 to 4 and 11 to 13 from row 2, joined along rows 7 and 8, the rest empty.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/lightning_around_reference.py`**, which works document 21's D-329 rule on top of D-324's reference in double precision. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/lightning_around/expected_lightning_around.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. After Effects' manual says only that its bolt goes round shapes and that a negative Alpha Obstacle keeps it inside them; the way round is this program's own rule, and no After Effects frame was compared.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks that path split, and path around with Alpha Obstacle 0, give every FX-LIGHTX case's bolt segment for segment (001, 002); that no reached segment sits within 1e-5 of a fork's cliff, nor a fork's side within 1e-5 of 0; that with path around no point of a main bolt is in a blocking pixel; that split stops at the block and around goes round it to the bottom edge, its middle untouched (003, 004), the forks stopped (005); that with no way in the bolt ends at the free pixel nearest the end point (006, 007); that a negative obstacle keeps a split bolt inside the block (008) and stops it leaving the U (009), while around follows the U to its other arm, the sky between untouched (010); and that half covering keeps the bolt at -40 and blocks its start at -60 (011, 012).

FX-LIGHTA-001 (`fx_lighta_001.json`): FX-LIGHTX-004 with the new word written at its starting value (path split): exactly FX-LIGHTX-004.

### Lightning Bolt's soft core (D-334)

From P-26's tutorial 2 (B-215). Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/lightning_core/`, holding D-324's `night.png` (the left half a night sky #1e2850, the right half empty) with one Lightning Bolt (`core.lightning_bolt`) on it, D-324's five settings and the new word `core` written. **Every number is produced by `tools/lightning_core_reference.py`** and is in `Fixtures/lightning_core/expected_lightning_core.json`. Values are linear premultiplied. Tolerance 2e-5. The line cases run along y = 4.5, the middle of row 4, from (-10, 45) to (110, 45) per cent, white in D-190's blue glow, jaggedness 0, no branches. B-215 checks them in `verification/D-334_lightning_core_table.md`.

FX-LCORE-001 (`fx_lcore_001.json`): The line at width 6, no glow, core soft. Down column 12 (on the empty half) the covering is 0, 0.041667, 0.333333, 0.666667, 0.916667, 0.666667, 0.333333, 0.041667, 0, 0 from row 0: brightest on row 4, 1 - 1/12 of white, fading to nothing past rows 1 and 7. Pixel (12, 4) is 0.916667 0.916667 0.916667 0.916667.

FX-LCORE-002 (`fx_lcore_002.json`): FX-LCORE-001 with core written "hard": D-190's core, rows 2 to 6 fully lit and rows 1 and 7 half, exactly D-324's frame for the same line.

FX-LCORE-003 (`fx_lcore_003.json`): FX-BOLT-001's settings with core soft, frames 0 and 2: the same bolt and glow as FX-BOLT-001, the core dimmer toward its edge and never brighter. On frame 0, 50 pixels differ from FX-BOLT-001's; the most, at (5, 0), is 0.424896 0.499955 1.02262 1 where the hard core gives 0.987643 0.998758 1.07774 1.

FX-LCORE-004 (`fx_lcore_004.json`): The line at width 1, core soft: row 4 half lit, pixel (12, 4) 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5.

FX-LCORE-005 (`fx_lcore_005.json`): The line at width 0 with glow 3, core soft: no core, only D-190's glow, exactly the hard core's frame.

FX-LCORE-006 (`fx_lcore_006.json`): A core "Soft": the word is exact, so a capital is not it. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning. Warning `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`. Frames 0 and 4: the night drawing untouched.

FX-LCORE-007 (`fx_lcore_007.json`): A core "fuzzy", which is not one. As FX-LCORE-006.

### Lightning Bolt's long forks (D-338)

From P-26's tutorial 2 (B-218). Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/lightning_forks/`, holding D-324's `night.png` (the left half a night sky #1e2850, the right half empty) with one Lightning Bolt (`core.lightning_bolt`) on it, D-324's five settings and the new word `forks` written. **Every number is produced by `tools/lightning_forks_reference.py`** and is in `Fixtures/lightning_forks/expected_lightning_forks.json`. Values are linear premultiplied. Tolerance 2e-5. The down cases run from the middle of the top edge to the middle of the bottom, white, width 1, no glow, branches 100 (D-324's FX-LIGHTX-005 bolt). B-218 checks them in `verification/D-338_lightning_forks_table.md`.

FX-LFORK-001 (`fx_lfork_001.json`): The down bolt with forks long, frames 0 and 1: the seven forks of the first three halvings each run on to the bottom edge beside the main bolt, turned 10 to 30 degrees from straight down, ending at at least three different places. On frame 0, 34 pixels differ from FX-LFORK-002's; on the bottom row, which D-324's forks leave dark past column 8, columns 9 to 12 are lit, (11, 9) 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5.

FX-LFORK-002 (`fx_lfork_002.json`): FX-LFORK-001 with forks written "short": D-324's forks, exactly FX-LIGHTX-005's bolt with branches 100.

FX-LFORK-003 (`fx_lfork_003.json`): FX-LFORK-001 with decay 50: each long fork goes half of what is left of the way down and thins to half its starting weight, so none reaches the bottom row past column 8.

FX-LFORK-004 (`fx_lfork_004.json`): FX-LFORK-001 over a drawing whose rows 7 to 9 are ground, Alpha Obstacle 50, frames 0 and 1: every strand stops where it reaches the ground. On frame 0 row 7 is lit at columns 4 to 9, on frame 1 at columns 6 to 11; rows 8 and 9 are the ground untouched. Tutorial 2's strands touching down.

FX-LFORK-005 (`fx_lfork_005.json`): FX-LFORK-001 as Strike: the long forks leave along the main bolt's own way too, so they are FX-LFORK-001's; only the short ones turn from the way to the end point, and 5 pixels differ from FX-LFORK-001's.

FX-LFORK-006 (`fx_lfork_006.json`): FX-BOLT-001's settings (branches 30) with forks long, frames 0 and 2: the same main bolt, the forks of its first three halvings longer. On frame 0, 3 pixels differ from FX-BOLT-001's, the most at (6, 9) 0.640998 0.687913 1.01529 1 where FX-BOLT-001 has 0.239058 0.327766 0.945138 1; on frame 2, 14, the most at (12, 8) 1 1 1 1 where FX-BOLT-001 has 0.122777 0.206496 0.787401 0.787401.

FX-LFORK-007 (`fx_lfork_007.json`): A forks "Long": the word is exact, so a capital is not it. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning. Warning `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`. Frames 0 and 4: the night drawing untouched.

FX-LFORK-008 (`fx_lfork_008.json`): A forks "many", which is not one. As FX-LFORK-007.

### CC Vector Blur (D-336)

From P-26's tutorial 2 (B-220). Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10, five frames, in `Fixtures/vector_blur/`: the drawing `holder` (two-pixel squares of red, blue and cream, its bottom right corner 4 by 3 clear) with the effect, and under it the map layers `ramp` (black to white left to right, moved, scaled and switched off), `disc` (a white disc of radius 3.5 on black) and `black`, a solid, all switched off. **Every number is produced by `tools/vector_blur_reference.py`** and is in `Fixtures/vector_blur/expected_vector_blur.json`. Values are linear premultiplied. Tolerance 2e-5. No slope in these cases lies within 1% of the flat line 1/10000. B-220 checks them in `verification/D-336_vector_blur_table.md`.

FX-VBLUR-001 (`fx_vblur_001.json`): As added: Natural, Amount 10, Ridge Smoothness 10, the layer's own lightness as the map, Map Softness 30: a soft smear along the slopes of its blurred brightness. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-002 (`fx_vblur_002.json`): Amount 0: nothing moves. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-003 (`fx_vblur_003.json`): The ramp as the map, Constant Length, Amount 3, Map Softness 0: its slope runs left to right, so rows 1 to 8 are smeared straight across, 3 pixels each way, evenly. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-004 (`fx_vblur_004.json`): The same as Natural, Ridge Smoothness 10: the ramp's gentle slope, 1/15 a pixel, makes the smear 3 * 6.67 / sqrt(6.67^2 + 10^2), 1.66 pixels each way, fading. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-005 (`fx_vblur_005.json`): The same as Perpendicular: along the slope's contour, so rows are left alone and columns smeared up and down. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-006 (`fx_vblur_006.json`): Natural with Angle Offset 90: exactly Perpendicular, FX-VBLUR-005. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-007 (`fx_vblur_007.json`): A black solid as the map, Direction Center, Angle Offset 90, Amount 3: the height is 0 everywhere, so every pixel is smeared 3 pixels each way across, evenly; rows 1 to 8 are FX-VBLUR-003. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-008 (`fx_vblur_008.json`): The same as Direction Fading: only forward, from the pixels to the right. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-009 (`fx_vblur_009.json`): The ramp with Direction Center, Revolutions 1, Amount 2: the direction turns once round from black to white, straight up at the left. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-010 (`fx_vblur_010.json`): FX-VBLUR-004 with Map Softness 4: the ramp's edges soften, so the slope bends near them. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-011 (`fx_vblur_011.json`): A white disc as the map, Natural, Ridge Smoothness 0, Map Softness 0, Amount 2: smeared in and out across its rim, and nowhere else. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-012 (`fx_vblur_012.json`): The disc as Perpendicular: smeared round its rim. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-013 (`fx_vblur_013.json`): Property Alpha on the layer itself, Constant Length, Amount 2, Map Softness 0: only the pixels on the drawing's edges and round its clear corner have a slope. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-014 (`fx_vblur_014.json`): Property Hue on the layer itself, Ridge Smoothness 5, Amount 3, Map Softness 2. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-015 (`fx_vblur_015.json`): Property Saturation on the layer itself, Constant Length, Amount 2, Map Softness 2. Frames 0.

FX-VBLUR-016 (`fx_vblur_016.json`): FX-VBLUR-003 with Amount keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 6 at frame 4: frame 0 untouched and frame 2 is FX-VBLUR-003. Frames 0, 2, 4.

### Moment Map (D-347)

After After Effects' Time Displacement (B-227). Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 10 frames a second, twelve frames, in `Fixtures/time_displacement/`: the drawing `holder`, twelve drawings one a frame (drawing k: red 20 k, green 10 + 15 x, blue 10 + 24 y, its bottom right 4 by 3 clear), with the effect; under it the map layers, all switched off: `ramp` (grey 17 x in column x, black to white), `ramp_dark` (the ramp with an Exposure of -1), `steps` (4 by 2 greys), `veil` (white at covering 128) and `orange` (a solid, linear 1, 0.25, 0). **Every number is produced by `tools/time_displacement_reference.py`** and is in `Fixtures/time_displacement/expected_time_displacement.json`. Values are linear premultiplied. Tolerance 2e-5. No moment in these cases lies within a thousandth of a step of a half, where rounding could tip. B-227 checks them in `verification/D-347_moment_map_table.md`.

FX-TDISP-001 (`fx_tdisp_001.json`): As added: Max Displacement 1 second, Time Resolution 60, the layer's own brightness as the map, Stretch: each pixel from a moment chosen by its own brightness; moments past the layer's twelve frames are clear. Frames 6.

FX-TDISP-002 (`fx_tdisp_002.json`): The ramp as the map, black at the left to white at the right, Max 0.5: column x is 4 x - 30 sixtieths of a second from now, so column 0 shows frame 1 and column 15 frame 11 at frame 6; at frame 0 the left half asks for frames before the layer, clear. Frames 0, 6.

FX-TDISP-003 (`fx_tdisp_003.json`): The same at Max -0.5: the other way, the left shows the frames after. Frames 6.

### Pass Extract and Depth Key (D-348)

After After Effects' 3D Channel Extract and Depth Matte (B-228; EFFECTS.md P0-5, a render's extra EXR channels). Every case is a project of one composition 8 by 6 at 24 frames a second, five frames, in `Fixtures/depth_channel/`: the layer `scene`, an EXR still. `media/scene.exr` holds half colour (red 0.1 + 0.1 x, green 0.2 + 0.05 y, blue 0.5; (0, 0) at half covering, (1, 0) clear), a float depth `Z` = 0.5 + 1.25 x + 0.75 y (exactly 6 at (2, 4)) and half normals `N.x` = (x - 3.5) / 4, `N.y` = (2.5 - y) / 3, `N.z` the rest of a unit length. `media/names.exr` names them `depth.Z` (20 - 2 x - y) and `normal.R`, `normal.G`, `normal.B`; `media/far.exr` has an infinity, a minus infinity and a not-a-number in its depth; `media/offset.exr` has its data window at columns 2 to 6 of rows 1 to 4; `media/plain.exr` has colour only; `media/card.png` is a PNG. **Every number is produced by `tools/depth_channel_reference.py`**, which writes and reads the files with OpenEXR's own library, and is in `Fixtures/depth_channel/expected_depth_channel.json`. Values are linear premultiplied. Tolerance 2e-5. A case's `frame_warning` is said at every frame it draws and not on opening. `Fixtures/depth_channel/sample/spheres.exr`, 320 by 180, is the playtest's picture, pinned by no number. B-228 checks them in `verification/D-348_depth_channels_table.md`.

### ID Key, ids, named channels and Blender's files (D-349)

After After Effects' ID Matte and EXtractoR (B-229; EFFECTS.md P0-5 part 2). The same compositions as D-348's above, in `Fixtures/depth_channel/`. `media/blender.exr` is `media/scene.exr` laid out as Blender writes a multilayer file: no plain R, G, B; the colour in `ViewLayer.Combined.R`, `.G`, `.B`, `.A`, the depth `ViewLayer.Depth.Z`, the normals `ViewLayer.Normal.X`, `.Y`, `.Z`, the object id `ViewLayer.IndexOB.X` (3 by 3 blocks, 0 to 5), the material id `ViewLayer.IndexMA.X` (diagonals, with 2.4 and 2.6 to test the half) and a mist `ViewLayer.Mist.Z`. `media/ids.exr` has a bare `ObjectID` (the column, 0 to 3) and `materialID.R`, `.G`, `.B` (7 or 8 by row; 100; 200). The rules are D-349's in `tools/depth_channel_reference.py`, which writes and reads the files with OpenEXR's own library; the numbers are in `Fixtures/depth_channel/expected_depth_channel.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. `Fixtures/depth_channel/sample/spheres_blender.exr`, 320 by 180, is the playtest's picture in Blender's layout, with object ids (the balls 1, 2, 3, the floor 4, the sky 0), material ids and a mist, pinned by no number. B-229 checks them in `verification/D-349_id_key_table.md`.

### Text animators (D-350)

After After Effects' text animators and Range Selector (B-230; EFFECTS.md P0-7 part 1). The rule is D-350's in `tools/text_animator_reference.py`, which reads the bundled M PLUS Rounded 1c with fontTools, never the build's ttf-parser, and finds each outline's box from its curves. For every character of every case, `Fixtures/text_animator/expected_text_animator.json` gives its unit, picked amount, move, turn, scale, opacity, colour, pen place and outline box; the numbers are held to 1e-6 and a box to 0.25 pixel, as the build fills straight pieces about 2 pixels long (D-263). Every case is a 1280 by 360 composition of one text layer under an identity transform. B-230 checks them, and draws the playtest's pictures, in `verification/D-350_text_animator_table.md`.

FX-TXA-001: Typewriter, hard, on "Typewriter text": Opacity 0, Start 40 of 15 characters, Smoothness 0. The first six show; the rest are not drawn.

FX-TXA-002: Typewriter, soft: Start 43.3, Smoothness 100. The seventh character half picked, half faded.

FX-TXA-003: Fade in by character: Opacity 0, Ramp Up, Ease High and Low 50, Offset -30. The left letters show, a soft edge, the right hidden.

FX-TXA-004: Fade out: Ramp Down, Offset 30.

FX-TXA-006: A wave: Position 0, -60, Start 20, End 50, Offset 10, Triangle. The letters in the range rise, most in its middle.

FX-TXA-007: Smooth and Round: a Smooth hump of Position 0, -40 over Start 0 to End 60, Offset 20, and a Round one of Scale 150 over the whole line.

FX-TXA-008: Turn, stretch, room and colour: Rotation 30, Scale 150 by 50 on all; then Rotation -10, Tracking 50, Fill on in green on the second half; faux italic, centred at 640.

### Stretch Levels, Stretch Contrast, Stretch Color and Spread Tones (D-351)

After After Effects' Auto Levels, Auto Contrast, Auto Color and Equalize (B-231; EFFECTS.md P0-15). Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, eight frames, in `Fixtures/auto_tone/`: the layer `holder` (effect `fx-1`; a Levels `fx-0` before it or `fx-2` after it where a case says so), a run of drawings flickering in brightness, 1, 2, 3, 1, 4, 5, 4, 5, with a cut at frame 4. Drawings 1 to 3 are a dull, warm picture (a grey ramp 70 to 188, red raised 20, blue lowered 25, an orange and a blue patch in the bottom rows, column 0 empty, column 15 at half covering), 2 lifted 12 and 3 lowered 10; drawings 4 and 5 a darker, cold ramp 20 to 131 with blue raised, 5 lifted 8. FX-AUTO-022 and 023 put the effect on an adjustment layer `adjust` above the holder. **Every number is produced by `tools/auto_tone_reference.py`**, which counts with numpy from the drawings' 8-bit values in double precision and asserts no value, running total or scene difference lies near an edge; the numbers are in `Fixtures/auto_tone/expected_auto_tone.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. B-231 checks them, and draws the playtest's pictures, in `verification/D-351_auto_tone_table.md`.

### Matte Choker, Refine Hard Matte and Refine Soft Matte (D-352)

After After Effects' Matte Choker, Refine Hard Matte and Refine Soft Matte (B-232; EFFECTS.md P0-20). Every case is a project of one composition 24 by 16 at 24 fps, five frames, in `Fixtures/matte_refine/`: the layer `art` holding the drawing `media/subject.png`, unmoved unless the case says, with the effect `fx-0-0`. The drawing: an orange disc about (11, 8) on a teal ramp; the matte a hard rectangle, columns 6 to 16 and rows 3 to 13, holding the disc and a ring of the teal, with a one-pixel hole at (11, 8); its right edge, column 17, at half covering; a speck of orange at (20, 2); and strands in columns 1 to 3, rows 4 to 11, orange and teal by turns down the rows, at coverings 64, 160 and 224. **Every number is produced by `tools/matte_refine_reference.py`**, which works in double precision with numpy from the drawing's 8-bit values and asserts no hard threshold lies near an edge; the numbers are in `Fixtures/matte_refine/expected_matte_refine.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. B-232 checks them, and draws the playtest's pictures, in `verification/D-352_matte_refine_table.md`.

FX-MREF-001 (`fx_mref_001.json`): Matte Choker as added: stage 1 geometric softness 4, choke 75, gray level softness 10 per cent; stage 2 geometric softness 0, choke 0, gray level softness 100 per cent; one iteration. The rectangle is choked in from its edges and its corners rounded; the speck, the strands and the half-covered edge go; the hole at (11, 8) fills, in the orange about it. Frames 0.

FX-MREF-002 (`fx_mref_002.json`): Matte Choker spreading then choking: stage 1 geometric softness 3, choke -60, gray level softness 20; stage 2 geometric softness 3, choke 60, gray level softness 20. The hole fills and the strands join, then the edges come back in. Frames 0.

FX-MREF-003 (`fx_mref_003.json`): Matte Choker with both stages at geometric softness 0, choke 0, gray level softness 100: each pixel's disc is itself and the ramp runs 0 to 1, so the output is the drawing. Frames 0.

FX-MREF-004 (`fx_mref_004.json`): Matte Choker, stage 1 geometric softness 2, choke 10, gray level softness 0: a hard step, every pixel covered in full where more than 54 per cent of its disc is covered and empty elsewhere. Frames 0.

FX-MREF-005 (`fx_mref_005.json`): Matte Choker, stage 1 geometric softness 2, choke 0, gray level softness 100: the covering is the disc's average, a soft blur of the matte that spreads into the empty pixels round it. Frames 0.

FX-MREF-006 (`fx_mref_006.json`): Matte Choker, stage 1 geometric softness 1.5, choke -40, gray level softness 50, three iterations: each pass spreads the matte further, though a lone corner can thin. Frames 0.

FX-MREF-007 (`fx_mref_007.json`): Matte Choker, stage 1 choke keyed from -100 at frame 0 to 100 at frame 4: frame 2 is choke 0. Frames 0, 2, 4.

### Soft Physical Glow (D-353)

The shared soft-glow engine (EFFECTS.md P0-21) and pick #1, Soft Physical Glow: Glow (`core.glow`) with the setting `falloff` written "physical" (B-233). Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames, in `Fixtures/soft_glow/`: the layer `art` holding a drawing the same size, unmoved unless the case says, with the effect `fx-0-0`. The drawings: `media/patches.png`, three patches in rows 3 to 6 on nothing, warm yellow in columns 2 to 4, brown in 7 and 8 and purple in 11 to 13; `media/faint.png`, the same at half covering; and `media/grey.png`, the brown swapped for a grey. **Every number is produced by `tools/soft_glow_reference.py`**, which works in double precision with numpy over whole padded planes of cells, from the drawings' 8-bit values, and asserts no hard threshold lies near an edge; the numbers are in `Fixtures/soft_glow/expected_soft_glow.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. B-233 checks them, and draws the playtest's pictures, in `verification/D-353_soft_glow_table.md`.

FX-SGLOW-001 (`fx_sglow_001.json`): Radius 12, everything else at the effect's defaults (threshold 0, so everything glows; Screen; exposure 1): a soft glow with a bright core and a long tail spreads round every patch into the empty space. Frames 0.

FX-SGLOW-002 (`fx_sglow_002.json`): The effect's own defaults, radius 500: the glow is spread so wide that on a drawing this small it is a faint wash; the drawing shows through brighter where it doubles on itself. Frames 0.

FX-SGLOW-003 (`fx_sglow_003.json`): Radius 0: nothing spreads; the light is laid on itself, so each pixel is doubled and held at white. Frames 0.

FX-SGLOW-004 (`fx_sglow_004.json`): Radius 1.5: the first level is too small to count yet, so this is still FX-SGLOW-003. Frames 0.

FX-SGLOW-005 (`fx_sglow_005.json`): Radius 2.25: the first level is half in, so the glow is half spread and half laid on itself. Frames 0.

FX-SGLOW-006 (`fx_sglow_006.json`): Radius 100: seven levels, the larger three worked on cells of 8, 4 and 2 pixels. Frames 0.

FX-SGLOW-007 (`fx_sglow_007.json`): Threshold 30, Chroma: each channel tested on its own: the yellow's red and green glow and its blue does not, the brown's red glows, the purple does not glow. Frames 0.

FX-SGLOW-012 (`fx_sglow_012.json`): Saturation Bias 50, threshold 40: halfway: the colourful patches glow in every channel, the grey, bright as it is, does not. Frames 0.

### Bilateral Blur (D-358)

Bilateral Blur (`core.bilateral_blur`), after After Effects' Bilateral Blur (B-237). Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames, in `Fixtures/bilateral_blur/`: the layer `art` holding D-203's specks drawing the same size (skin with specks, a hole, a line two pixels wide, a patch of grain eight levels either side of the skin, and a column at half covering; `Fixtures/bilateral_blur/media/specks.png`), unmoved unless the case says, with the effect `fx-0-0`. **Every number is produced by `tools/bilateral_blur_reference.py`**, which weighs every tap of every pixel's disc in double precision from the drawing's 8-bit values; the numbers are in `Fixtures/bilateral_blur/expected_bilateral_blur.json`. Tolerance 2e-5. The tool checks what the cases claim: the line and the dark specks kept to a tenth of a level at the defaults, the grain's spread more than halved, the white speck still light, Colorize off grey everywhere with every covering kept, Radius 0 and Threshold 0 the drawing exactly, Threshold 255 a soft blur that stays inside the drawing, and the keyed frames. B-237 checks them, and draws the playtest's pictures, in `verification/D-358_bilateral_blur_table.md`.

FX-BILAT-001 (`fx_bilat_001.json`): Bilateral Blur as it starts, Radius 5, Threshold 20, Colorize on: the grain, 8 levels either side of the skin, is smoothed toward the skin, while the line and the dark specks, far more than 20 from the skin, stay as they are to well within a level; the white speck, 41 and 65 from the skin in green and blue, stays far lighter than the skin. The hole stays a hole and the half-covered column keeps its half covering. Frames 0.

FX-BILAT-002 (`fx_bilat_002.json`): Radius 0: the drawing, untouched. Frames 0.

FX-BILAT-003 (`fx_bilat_003.json`): Threshold 0: each pixel counts only itself, so the drawing is unchanged. Frames 0.

FX-BILAT-004 (`fx_bilat_004.json`): Colorize off: the same smoothing worked on luminance alone, and every pixel that shows is grey, red, green and blue equal; the line stays dark and the outline is kept. Frames 0.

FX-BILAT-005 (`fx_bilat_005.json`): Colorize off with Radius 0: no smoothing, each pixel only its own luminance, grey. Frames 0.

FX-BILAT-006 (`fx_bilat_006.json`): Threshold 255: likeness hardly matters, a soft blur that stays inside the drawing: the line and the specks are blurred into the skin, and the hole, the empty column and the empty row stay empty. Frames 0.

### Text shaping (D-371)

Words shaped by `rustybuzz` (B-250; EFFECTS.md P0-7 part 2). The rule is D-371's in `tools/text_shaping_reference.py`, which shapes with HarfBuzz itself (`uharfbuzz` 0.53.3) and reads outlines with fontTools, never the build's code. `Fixtures/text_shaping/expected_text_shaping.json` gives, for FX-SHAPE-001 to 012, every glyph left to right as its number in the font, its advance, its two offsets and the character its cluster starts at, whole font units held exactly; and for FX-SHAPE-020 to 023 every character's anchor, to 1e-6, and the exact box of its cluster's outline, to 0.25 pixel, or none for a character that is not the first of its cluster. The fonts are the bundled M PLUS Rounded 1c and, for Arabic and Devanagari, which it lacks, Noto Sans Arabic 2.013 and Noto Sans Devanagari 2.007 in `Fixtures/text_shaping/fonts` (SIL Open Font License 1.1). B-250 checks them, and draws the layout cases' pictures, in `verification/D-371_text_shaping_table.md`.

FX-SHAPE-001: Arabic joins: "as-salamu alaykum" in Noto Sans Arabic, kerning off. One right-to-left run; every letter takes its joined form, lam and alef in "salam" the lam-alef pair. 13 glyphs.

FX-SHAPE-002: The same with kerning on.

FX-SHAPE-003: Arabic vowel marks: "bismi" with kasra, sukun and kasra, each mark over or under its letter by the font's offsets, with no width of its own. 7 glyphs.

FX-SHAPE-004: Devanagari: "namaste hindi". The conjunct sta is one glyph; the i-matra of hi is drawn before its consonant; nda is a conjunct. 11 glyphs.

FX-SHAPE-005: Devanagari: ksha and shri, each a conjunct. 4 glyphs.

FX-SHAPE-006: Latin ligatures in the bundled font, kerning off: "office fly fit staff". ffi, fl, fi and ff are each one glyph, held by their first letter. 15 glyphs.

FX-SHAPE-007: The same with kerning on (the font kerns "ta" and "st").

FX-SHAPE-008: A combining accent typed after its letter: "cafe" then U+0301. The font has e-acute, so the two become that one glyph.

FX-SHAPE-009: Accents with no precomposed letter: A with acute and diaeresis, x with dot below and acute; each mark a glyph of no width in its letter's cluster.

FX-SHAPE-010: A mixed line, left-to-right paragraph: "Hi salam". "Hi " left to right, then the Arabic right to left where it stands. Noto Sans Arabic has no Latin letters, so H and i are its missing glyph.

FX-SHAPE-011: A mixed line, right-to-left paragraph: "salam Hi". The Arabic with the space after it is drawn on the right, Hi on the left.

FX-SHAPE-012: Figures after Arabic, right-to-left paragraph: "salam 2026". The figures read left to right, drawn to the left of the Arabic.

FX-SHAPE-020: "office fly fit staff" at 100 pixels from 100, 200 with tracking 50, kerning off: each ligature drawn at its first letter, the other letters in it with no outline. The reference's boxes slide each outline to its hmtx side bearing, as FreeType does, and since D-372 (a) (B-251) the build does too; before it, "y" differed by 0.4 pixel and the row was in dispute.

FX-SHAPE-021: "as-salamu alaykum" at 120 pixels from 80, 240: the first letter typed on the right, the last on the left.

FX-SHAPE-022: "bismi" at 200 pixels from 60, 300: each vowel mark over or under its letter, inside the letter's cluster.

FX-SHAPE-023: "namaste hindi" at 120 pixels from 40, 200: the i-matra drawn before its consonant, both in the cluster of the consonant typed first.

## Compound Blur fixtures

D-191, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/compound_blur/`. At the top is the drawing `holder`, `Fixtures/compound_blur/media/holder.png`, two-pixel squares of red #dc2828, blue #2850dc and cream #f0f0c8 in turn, `(x div 2 + y div 2) mod 3`, its bottom right corner, columns 12 to 15 of rows 7 to 9, clear; it holds one Compound Blur (`core.compound_blur`), unless the case puts it on an adjustment layer. Under it are the map layers, every one switched off, so only the holder is seen: `ramp`, `media/ramp.png`, grey 17 x in column x, black at the left to white at the right, moved to (3, 2) and scaled to 50 %; the solids `white`, `black` and `grey` (linear 0.25), 16 by 10; `card`, `media/card.png`, a 4 by 2 checker of white and black, white at its top left; and `late`, a white solid whose in point is frame 4. Each value is a pixel's four working numbers, linear and premultiplied, red, green, blue and covering.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/compound_blur_reference.py`**, which works D-191's rule in double precision at every pixel, the Gaussian summed directly in two dimensions, from the drawings' 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/compound_blur/expected_compound_blur.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks that no map, a black map, Maximum Blur 0, a missing layer and a layer before its in point leave the drawing exactly (001, 004, 009, 015, 016); that a white map, a black one inverted and a late one inverted are the Gaussian at sigma 2 (003, 005, 017); that the ramp leaves column 0 sharp and blurs column 15 the most, and inverted the other way round (002, 006); that repeated edges change the picture and not the sharp column (008); that the centred checker touches only the eight pixels it covers (010); that tiled and stretched differ (011, 012); that the holder's own clear corner stays clear (013); that the keyed frame 2 is 002 (014); that the moved holder is 002 moved (018); that the adjustment layer is 002 (019); and that no case takes the covering outside 0 and 1.

FX-CBLUR-001: As added: no layer named, so nothing is blurred.

Frame 0: every pixel is the drawing's, unchanged.

FX-CBLUR-002: The ramp as the map, Maximum Blur 6: sharp at the left, blurred more and more to the right. The ramp layer is moved, scaled and switched off, none of which the map reads.

## Displacement Map fixtures

D-193, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/displacement_map/`. On top is the drawing `holder`, `Fixtures/displacement_map/media/holder.png`, Compound Blur's: two-pixel squares of red #dc2828, blue #2850dc and cream #f0f0c8 in turn, `(x div 2 + y div 2) mod 3`, its bottom right corner, columns 12 to 15 of rows 7 to 9, clear. It holds one Displacement Map (`core.displacement_map`), unless the case puts it on an adjustment layer above it. Beneath it are the map layers, every one switched off, so only the holder is seen: `ramp`, `media/ramp.png`, grey 17 x in column x, moved to (3, 2) and scaled to 50 %; the solids `white` and `black`, 16 by 10; `card`, `media/card.png`, a 4 by 2 checker of white and black, white at its top left; `paint`, `media/paint.png`, 16 by 10, the colour (40 + 8 y, 30 + 14 x, 200 - 12 x + 3 y) of 255, greens and blues; `veil`, `media/veil.png`, 16 by 10, white with covering 28 y of 255; and `late`, a white solid whose in point is frame 4. Each value is a pixel's four working numbers, linear and premultiplied, red, green, blue and covering.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/displacement_map_reference.py`**, which works D-193's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawings' 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/displacement_map/expected_displacement_map.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks that no map, both directions Off, a missing layer, a layer before its in point and a maximum keyed to 0 leave the drawing exactly (001, 007, 019, 020, 018); that a white map moves the picture 2 left and 2 up, a black one 2 right and 2 down, negative maxima make white act as black, Full moves it whatever the map, Wrap brings back what leaves, and the late map at frame 4 is the white one (003 to 006, 013, 020); that the ramp's black column reads 2 left and 2 up and its white column 2 right and 2 down (002); that the keyed frame 2 moves across as the ramp does at 2 (018); that Wrap changes only the edges (023); that a clear map moves nothing and a clear map read by alpha reads off the picture (011, 012); that the centred checker moves only the eight pixels it covers (014); that tiled and stretched differ (015, 016); that the holder's clear corner stays clear (017); that the moved holder is 002 moved (021); that the adjustment layer is 002 (022); that the three painted cases each move the picture, differently (008 to 010); and that no case takes the covering outside 0 and 1.

FX-DMAP-001: As added: no layer named, so nothing moves.

Frame 0: every pixel is the drawing's, unchanged.

## Gradient Wipe fixtures

D-194, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/gradient_wipe/`. On top is the drawing `holder`, `Fixtures/gradient_wipe/media/holder.png`, Compound Blur's: two-pixel squares of red #dc2828, blue #2850dc and cream #f0f0c8 in turn, `(x div 2 + y div 2) mod 3`, its bottom right corner, columns 12 to 15 of rows 7 to 9, clear. It holds one Gradient Wipe (`core.gradient_wipe`), unless the case puts it on an adjustment layer above it. Beneath it are the map layers, every one switched off, so only the holder is seen: `ramp`, `media/ramp.png`, grey 17 x in column x, moved to (3, 2) and scaled to 50 %; the solids `white` and `black`, 16 by 10; `card`, `media/card.png`, a 4 by 2 checker of white and black, white at its top left; `veil`, `media/veil.png`, 16 by 10, white with covering 28 y of 255; and `late`, a white solid whose in point is frame 4. Each value is a pixel's four working numbers, linear and premultiplied, red, green, blue and covering.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/gradient_wipe_reference.py`**, which works D-194's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawings' 8-bit values, and stops if a pixel decided by a hard edge lies within 1e-5 of it. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/gradient_wipe/expected_gradient_wipe.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks that no map, completion 0, a white map at 99 and a missing layer leave the drawing exactly (001, 002, 005, 010, 019); that completion 100 at any softness, a black map at 1 and an empty map before its in point leave nothing (006, 007, 011, 020); that the ramp at 50 keeps its light half whole and none of its dark half, and inverted the other way round (003, 008); that at softness 100 each pixel is kept by the ramp's brightness, 17 x of 255 (004); that at 30 and softness 20 columns 0 to 2 go, 6 on stay whole and 3 to 5 fade (009); that the veil's two clearest rows go (012); that the centred checker keeps its four white pixels only and the tiled one a checker (013, 014); that the holder read by itself keeps only its cream (016); that the keyed frames are the cases they name (017, 018); that the moved holder is 003 moved and the adjustment layer is 003 (021, 022); and that no case adds to any number.

## Echo fixtures

D-195, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, eight frames long, in `Fixtures/echo/`, holding the drawn layer `holder` with one Echo (`core.echo`), unless the case puts it on an adjustment layer above. The holder shows the image sequence `run`, `Fixtures/echo/media/run_1.png` to `run_5.png`, each 14 by 5: a ball three pixels square in rows 1 to 3, its left column at 2 k - 1 in drawing k, coloured #e6 then (40 + 40 k) then (210 - 40 k) in hex, opaque, with the column behind it the same colour at covering 128 of 255, the rest clear. Drawings 1 to 4 are exposed one frame each and drawing 5 from frame 4 to the end, unless the case says otherwise. Each value is a pixel's four working numbers, linear and premultiplied, red, green, blue and covering.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/echo_reference.py`**, which works D-195's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawings' 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/echo/expected_echo.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks that no echoes at full intensity and the adjustment layer leave the drawing exactly (002, 021), and frame 0 of the first case, whose echo is before the layer (001); that Add is the sum of the named drawings held at 1 (001, 004, 005, 006, 013, 014, 022); that half intensity halves (003); that Minimum keeps only the two columns where two drawings meet (008); that Composite In Back has the present ball whole on top and In Front the oldest copy over the next (010, 011); that Blend is the average (012); that a part frame and a part echo count as the whole below (015, 016); that an Exposure before the Echo is not seen and one after it darkens all (017, 018); that the mask keeps nothing right of column 6 (019); that the moved holder is 001 moved (020); that keyed intensity 0 leaves nothing (023); and that every number of every case is between 0 and 1 with colour no more than covering.

## Posterize Time fixtures

D-196, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, eight frames long, in `Fixtures/posterize_time/`, holding the drawn layer `holder` with one Posterize Time (`core.posterize_time`), unless the case says otherwise. The holder shows the image sequence `ball`, `Fixtures/posterize_time/media/ball_1.png` to `ball_8.png`, each 14 by 5, drawing k exposed at frame k - 1: a ball three pixels square in rows 1 to 3, its left column at k, coloured #e6 then (20 + 25 k) then (220 - 25 k) in hex, opaque, with the column behind it the same colour at covering 128 of 255, the rest clear. Each value is a pixel's four working numbers, linear and premultiplied, red, green, blue and covering.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/posterize_time_reference.py`**, which works D-196's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawings' 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/posterize_time/expected_posterize_time.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks that each frame of each case is the drawing of the frame the case names, moved where the case moves it (001 to 008, 011, 012, 014 to 017); that the Exposure keyed before or after it is held at frame 2's +1 (009, 010); that the Echo after it is frame 2's and frame 1's drawings added, on both frames (013); that the wrong settings leave every frame as drawn (018 to 020); and that holding twice is holding once, at rates 0.1 to 24 in compositions of 24, 25, 30 and 23.976 for the first 200 frames.

## Change to Color fixtures

D-197, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 in `Fixtures/change_to_color/`, holding the still `Fixtures/change_to_color/media/swatches.png`, the same size, unmoved unless the case says, with one Change to Color (`core.change_to_color`). The drawing is a box of line #1e1a24 in columns 2 to 14 and rows 1 to 8 holding, in rows 2 to 7, one column each of #c82828 (a red), #8c1e28 (its shadow), #f08c8c (its highlight), #400808 (a dark red), #806060 (a dull red), #ff0040 (a pink), #dca08c (a skin's shadow), #f6d6be (a skin), #40c040, #4060ff and #808080, columns 3 to 13; down its left side, column 1, #c82828 at covering 128 of 255 in rows 1 to 4 and #4060ff at 128 in rows 5 to 8; the rest clear. Each value is a pixel's four working numbers, linear and premultiplied, red, green, blue and covering; only the pixels that differ from the drawing are listed, a run of rows holding the same pair once.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/change_to_color_reference.py`**, which works D-197's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/change_to_color/expected_change_to_color.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks that HLS goes there and back; that every case keeps each pixel's covering, leaves the clear pixels clear, and treats the half-covered red and blue as the full ones; that no distance lies within 1e-5 of a tolerance without a band; and each case's claim: which colours change whole, partly or not at all, what hue, lightness and saturation the changed ones reach, that the matte is white, grey or black where it should be, and that the keyed, moved and capitalised cases are the plain ones they name.

FX-CTC-001: The settings as they start: from #ff0000 to #0080ff, Hue, by setting, hue tolerance 5, lightness and saturation tolerance 50, softness 50. The red, its shadow 5.5 degrees round the wheel, its highlight, the dark red and the red at half covering take #0080ff's hue, each keeping its own lightness and saturation, so the shading stays; the dull red, too far from #ff0000's saturation, the pink and the skin's shadow, 15 degrees round, and every other colour are untouched.

## Corner Pin fixtures

D-198, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/corner_pin/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Corner Pin (`core.corner_pin`) on it, after a Motion Tile (`core.motion_tile`) at 300% by 300% where the case says, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is Wave Warp's, `Fixtures/corner_pin/media/stripes.png`: in rows 0 to 8 and columns 0 to 13, upright stripes two pixels wide, skin #f6d6be and line #1e1a24 by turns starting with skin, crossed by a blue band #3a6fd8 in rows 4 and 5, touching the drawing's top and left edges; column 14 is the skin at half covering, a soft edge; column 15 and row 9 are empty. The corners are written (x, y), in per cent of the drawing's width and height; a corner not named is where it starts. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that differ from the drawing, as the case moves it, are listed, a run of rows in one column holding the same pair once: every other pixel is the drawing's own, to 1e-12. A layer that grows is shown with its grown pixels in place.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/corner_pin_reference.py`**, which works D-198's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, the sampling by `tools/radial_blur_reference.py`'s bilinear rule and the tiling by `tools/motion_tile_reference.py`. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/corner_pin/expected_corner_pin.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks the rule's own pieces: the map carries the square's corners to the four points, the adjugate times the map is its determinant, the crossed, bent-in and in-line corners are refused and the others kept, and the growth is 0, 4, 64 or 40 pixels where it should be. It checks that every case keeps every pixel premultiplied with its covering in 0..1 and is the same with the layer grown far more, so the growth cuts nothing (all); and each case's claim: the drawing untouched as it starts (001); shrunk into columns 4 to 11 and rows 2 to 6 with everything else clear (002); the keystone's band in rows 2 and 3, its top row narrowed (003); an exact mirror and half turn (004, 005); the stretched corner in the three columns left of the drawing (006); the lower right clear (007); the crossed, bent-in and in-line corners clear (008 to 010); the keyed corners meeting the plain ones at their frames, the overshoot held at -400 (011, 012); the move and move back giving the drawing again (013); the tiles filling the frame and repeating every 8 columns and 5 rows (014); and the horizon at 1.78 pixels left of the drawing, clear to its left, where the map without the horizon test draws something (015).

FX-PIN-001: The settings as they start, the corners at (0, 0), (100, 0), (0, 100) and (100, 100): the drawing, untouched, and nothing grows.

Frame 0: every pixel is the drawing's.

## Light Sweep fixtures

D-199, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/light_sweep/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Light Sweep (`core.light_sweep`) on it, after a Motion Tile (`core.motion_tile`) at 300% by 300% where the case says, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is Rim Light's, `Fixtures/light_sweep/media/figure.png`: a block of skin #f6d6be in columns 3 to 12 and rows 2 to 7, its foot, row 7, line #1e1a24; the skin at half covering down column 2 beside it, a soft edge; and a red dot #c82828 alone at (14, 5). The rest is empty. The settings as they start are centre (50, 50), direction -30, smooth, width 50, sweep intensity 50, edge intensity 100, edge thickness 1, light colour #ffffff and light reception add; a case says what it changes, and "the band" is direction 0, linear, width 5, sweep intensity 100 and edge intensity 0. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that differ from the drawing, as the case moves it, are listed, a run of rows in one column holding the same pair once: every other pixel is the drawing's own, tiled where the case tiles it, to 1e-12.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/light_sweep_reference.py`**, which works D-199's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, the tiling by `tools/motion_tile_reference.py`. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/light_sweep/expected_light_sweep.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks the rule's own pieces: the three shapes' strengths at the band's pixels, 0 at width 0, and the directions exact at quarter turns. It checks that every case but the moved ones leaves the empty pixels as they are and that only cutout changes a covering (all); and each case's claim: every drawn pixel lit as it starts, the rims more than the middle (001); the drawing untouched at width 0 and at no intensity (002, 003); the band's columns gaining exactly 0.8 and 0.4, 0.896 and 0.352, and 1 and 0.5 of white by shape (004 to 006); rows 4 and 5 gaining two thirds (007); the leaning band (008); the edges alone, the column beside the soft edge half lit and the middle untouched, and two pixels deep at thickness 2.7 (009, 010); the orange added, composited and the cutout left alone, held at full on the edges (011 to 014); the keyed centre meeting the plain ones at its frames and the overshoot held at 100 (015, 016); a turn and a quarter the same as a quarter (017); the band moving with the layer (018); and the band crossing into the tile on the drawing's left, lighting columns 6 and 10 and nowhere else (019).

FX-SWEEP-001: The settings as they start: centre (50, 50), direction -30, smooth, width 50, sweep intensity 50, edge intensity 100, edge thickness 1, white, add. The band, wider than the frame, lights the whole figure, most along a line through the middle leaning left, and its edges most of all: the block's border, the soft edge and the lone red dot.

## Radio Waves fixtures

D-200, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/radio_waves/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Radio Waves (`core.radio_waves`) on it, after a Motion Tile (`core.motion_tile`) at 300% by 300% where the case says, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is Lightning Bolt's night, `Fixtures/radio_waves/media/night.png`: its left half, columns 0 to 7, a night sky #1e2850, and its right half empty. The settings as they start are producer point (50, 50), sides 64, interval 24, expansion 5, orientation 0, direction 90, velocity 0, spin 0, lifespan 96, opacity 100, fade-in 0, fade-out 48, start and end width 5, square and colour #ffffff; a case says what it changes, and "the ring" is sides 4, orientation 45, interval 10, expansion 2, lifespan 10, fade-out 0 and widths 1 and 1: one square, its sides 2.83 pixels from the middle at frame 2. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that differ from the drawing, as the case moves it, are listed, a run of rows in one column holding the same pair once: every other pixel is the drawing's own, tiled where the case tiles it, to 1e-12.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/radio_waves_reference.py`**, which works D-200's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, the tiling by `tools/motion_tile_reference.py`. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/radio_waves/expected_radio_waves.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks the rule's own pieces: the waves alive at a frame, the three profiles, the distance from a square's and a triangle's outline and the fades. It checks that every pixel is the drawing painted toward the colour by some share, the same share on its colour and its covering (all); and each case's claim: the first wave a solid dot in the middle, a ring only the corners reach at frame 2, and gone by frame 4 (001); nothing at opacity 0 or width 0 (002, 003); the ring even left to right and top to bottom, its side lines shared 0.672 and 0.328 between columns 4 and 5, and nothing inside or beyond (004); the triangle's foot half in rows 6 and 7 (005); spin, a turn and a quarter and 4.7 sides giving the ring exactly (006, 017, 020); the drift the same as a moved producer (007); three waves at once, and the oldest gone at lifespan 3, the rest unchanged (008, 009); the width halved halfway through life (010); the fades halving the ring (011); the triangle and sine profiles at column 5, the sine never dimmer (012, 013); the orange at half strength (014); the keyed producer meeting the plain ones at its frames and the overshoot held at 100 (015, 016); the ring moving with the layer (018); and the ring drawn across the tile and the drawing alike, even left to right (019).

At frame 0 the first wave is born, a white dot 5 pixels across in the middle; at frame 2 it is a ring 10 pixels out that only the frame's corners reach; by frame 4 it has left the frame.

## Polar Coordinates fixtures

D-201, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/polar_coordinates/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Polar Coordinates (`core.polar_coordinates`) on it, two where the case says, after a Motion Tile (`core.motion_tile`) at 300% by 300% where the case says, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is Wave Warp's, `Fixtures/polar_coordinates/media/stripes.png`: in rows 0 to 8 and columns 0 to 13, upright stripes two pixels wide, skin #f6d6be and line #1e1a24 by turns starting with skin, crossed by a blue band #3a6fd8 in rows 4 and 5, touching the drawing's top and left edges; column 14 is the skin at half covering, a soft edge; column 15 and row 9 are empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that differ from the drawing, as the case moves and tiles it, are listed, a run of rows in one column holding the same pair once: every other pixel is the drawing's own, to 1e-12.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/polar_coordinates_reference.py`**, which works D-201's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values, the sampling by `tools/radial_blur_reference.py`'s bilinear rule and the tiling by `tools/motion_tile_reference.py`. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/polar_coordinates/expected_polar_coordinates.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks the rule's own pieces: each conversion undoes the other, straight up from the middle reads the drawing's left edge, the right side a quarter across and the ellipse its foot, and the unrolled top-left corner reads the middle. It checks that every case keeps every pixel premultiplied with its covering in 0..1 (all); and each case's claim: the frame's corners clear, the band a ring halfway out and the middle the drawing's top row, and straight up from the middle part covered where, with the columns not taken round, it would be clear (001); the drawing untouched at 0 (002); the band along the top row, unrolled, and the stripes below (003); the halfway cases neither the drawing nor all the way (004, 005); the keyed interpolation meeting the plain cases at its frames and the overshoot held at 100 (006, 007); the move (008); inside the ellipse the tiled case the same as 001 and outside it the tiles drawn where 001 is clear (009); 003 in the drawing's place and its right half again to its left, all but the middle of the foot row, which reads the tile below (010); and the band back in rows 4 and 5, the top row and the edges soft (011).

FX-POLAR-001: The settings as they start, Interpolation 100 and Rect to Polar: the drawing bent round its middle. Its top row is squeezed into the middle, its blue band, rows 4 and 5, is a ring halfway out, and its foot, the empty row 9, lies round the ellipse that touches the frame's sides, so the frame's corners, beyond it, are clear. Its upright stripes are spokes from the middle, and its empty right-hand column is a clear spoke straight up.

### 32 bpc (After Effects) working depth (D-333)

From P-26 and the owner's approval of D-333 on 2026-10-06. After its step F tutorial 2 is in After Effects' 32 bpc, which by default has no linear working space: its blurs average display values, and Exposure, which the CS3 manual (p.402) says works "in a linear color space", is taken here to get there and back with a plain 2.2 curve. ## Mix fixtures

D-202, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps in `Fixtures/effect_mix/`, each effect's `mix` written on its record after `enabled` or not at all, as the case says. FX-MIX-001 to 012 and 014 to 016 hold Invert's drawing, `Fixtures/effect_mix/media/bands.png` (the drawing of FX-INVERT, described there), five frames long, unmoved, with Invert (`core.invert`, channel rgb, amount 100), Gaussian Blur (`core.gaussian_blur`, edges transparent) or Exposure (`core.exposure`) on it, or on an adjustment layer above it in 012. FX-MIX-013 is FX-WRAP-001's scene, Light Wrap's box `wrap_box.png` over its bands `wrap_bands.png`, the Light Wrap on the box. FX-MIX-017 is FX-PTIME-001's project, eight frames of the running ball `ball_1.png` to `ball_8.png`, its Posterize Time given a mix. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that differ from the case without the mixed effects (the drawing; for 013 the box over the bands unlit; for 017 the ball not held) are listed, a run of rows in one column holding the same pair once: every other pixel is as without them, to 1e-12.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/effect_mix_reference.py`**, which works D-202's rule in double precision at every pixel from the drawings' 8-bit values, Invert by `tools/invert_reference.py`'s rule, the blur by `tools/edges_reference.py`'s, the Light Wrap by `tools/light_wrap_reference.py`'s and the adjustment layer by `tools/adjust_reference.py`'s. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/effect_mix/expected_effect_mix.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks the rule's own pieces: at 100 the effect's result itself, at 0 its input placed in the grown rectangle, transparent round it, and at 50 half way. ## Median and Smart Blur fixtures

D-203, accepted on 2026-09-28. Every case is a project of one composition 16 by 10 at 24 fps, five frames long, in `Fixtures/median_smart_blur/`, holding one drawing the same size with one Median (`core.median`) or one Smart Blur (`core.smart_blur`) on it, unmoved unless the case says. The drawing is `Fixtures/median_smart_blur/media/specks.png`: in rows 0 to 8 and columns 0 to 13, skin #f6d6be crossed by an upright line #1e1a24 in columns 9 and 10; dark specks, the line's colour, at (2, 1) and (12, 4), a white speck #ffffff at (6, 2), and a hole, empty, at (12, 1); in rows 5 to 8 and columns 0 to 7 grain, the skin 8 lighter (#fedec6) or 8 darker (#eeceb6) at scattered pixels, row by row `+s-s+-s+`, `s-+s-s+-`, `-s+-s+s-` and `s+s-+s-+`, s the skin. Column 14 is the skin at half covering, a soft edge; column 15 and row 9 are empty. Values are linear premultiplied working values, and only the pixels that differ from the drawing, as the case moves it, are listed, a run of rows in one column holding the same pair once: every other pixel is the drawing's own, to 1e-12.

**Every number below is produced by `tools/median_smart_blur_reference.py`**, which works D-203's rules in double precision at every pixel from the drawing's 8-bit values. The same numbers are in `Fixtures/median_smart_blur/expected_median_smart_blur.json`. Tolerance 2e-5.

**Checked by what they claim.** The tool checks the rules' own pieces: the disc's sizes (one tap below radius 1, five at 1, nine at 1.5, thirteen at 2), the median of an odd and an even count, and the 8-bit levels of the white speck and the soft edge. It checks that every case keeps every pixel premultiplied with its covering in 0..1 (all); and each case's claim: the specks turned to skin, the line kept, the hole a hole, the soft column soft and most of the grain skin (MEDIAN-001); the drawing untouched at radius 0 (MEDIAN-002); specks gone and line kept at radius 1 (MEDIAN-003); the hole filled with skin and the top-left corner cut away with Operate on Alpha on (MEDIAN-004); the keyed radius meeting MEDIAN-001 at frame 2 (MEDIAN-005) and the overshoot held at 10, where every pixel that shows is the skin at its own covering (MEDIAN-006); the move (MEDIAN-007, SMART-008); the specks, the line and the soft column kept, the hole a hole and every grain pixel changed, the grain's spread from the skin less than half the drawing's (SMART-001); the drawing untouched at radius 0 and, to 1e-12, at threshold 0 (SMART-002, 003); the grain smoothed less at threshold 8 than at 64 (SMART-004); at 255 the specks and the line blurred while the hole, the empty column and the empty row stay empty (SMART-005); the keyed threshold meeting SMART-004 and SMART-001 (SMART-006); and the overshoot held at radius 10 (SMART-007).

FX-MEDIAN-001: Median as it starts, Radius 2 and Operate on Alpha off: the three specks are gone into the skin and the grain is mostly skin, while the line, two pixels wide, is kept, and so is the drawing's outline: the hole stays a hole and the half-covered column stays at half.
